the full-model determinism contract.\"\"\"\n    model, losses = train_model(config, device=device)\n    del model\n    return losses\n\n\ndef _train(config: Config) -> tuple[list[float], list[float]]:\n    if config.task != \"copy\":\n        raise ValueError(\"the Phase 0 trainer supports only task='copy'\")\n    if config.precision != \"fp32\":\n        raise ValueError(\"the Phase 0 trainer requires fp32\")\n\n    model = initialize_model(config).to(dtype=torch.float32)\n    operands = named_generator(config.seed_data, \"operands\")\n    # Instantiate the registered optimizer stream even though AdamW has no random draws.\n    named_generator(config.seed_train, \"train\")\n    decay = [model.embedding_weight, model.head_weight]\n    no_decay = [model.head_bias]\n    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(\n        [\n            {\"params\": decay, \"weight_decay\": config.weight_decay},\n            {\"params\": no_decay, \"weight_decay\": 0.0},\n        ],\n        lr=config.lr,\n        betas=(config.adam_beta1, config.adam_beta2),\n        eps=config.adam_eps,\n    )\n\n    losses: list[float] = []\n    learning_rates: list[float] = []\n    for step in range(config.steps):\n        lr = _learning_rate(config, step)\n        for group in optimizer.param_groups:\n            group[\"lr\"] = lr\n        tokens = _next_batch(config, operands)\n        logits = model(tokens)\n        loss = F.cross_entropy(\n            logits[:, 1:, :].reshape(-1, config.vocab),\n            tokens[:, :-1].reshape(-1),\n        )\n        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)\n        loss.backward()\n        nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), config.clip)\n        optimizer.step()\n        losses.append(loss.detach().item())\n        learning_rates.append(lr)\n    return losses, learning_rates\n\n\ndef _learning_rate(config: Config, step: int) -> float:\n    if step < config.warmup:\n        return config.lr * (step + 1) / config.warmup\n    decay_intervals = max(1, config.steps - config.warmup - 1)\n    progress = min(1.0, (step - config.warmup) / decay_intervals)\n    cosine = 0.5 * (1.0 + math.cos(math.pi * progress))\n    return config.lr_min + (config.lr - config.lr_min) * cosine\n\n\ndef run(\n    config: Config,\n    *,\n    repo: str | Path = \".\",\n    force: bool = False,\n    allow_dirty: bool = False,\n) -> Path:\n    root = Path(repo).resolve()\n    identity = git_identity(root)\n    if identity.dirty and not allow_dirty:\n        raise RuntimeError(\"dirty worktree requires --allow-dirty\")\n    identifier = make_run_id(config, identity)\n    run_dir = root / \"results\" / identifier\n    _prepare_run_dir(run_dir, identity, force)\n\n    (run_dir / \"config.json\").write_bytes(canonical_json(config.as_dict()) + b\"\\n\")\n    env = _environment(identity)\n    (run_dir / \"env.json\").write_bytes(canonical_json(env) + b\"\\n\")\n    if config.task == \"copy\":\n        losses, learning_rates = _train(config)\n        with (run_dir / \"metrics.jsonl\").open(\"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n            for step, (loss, lr) in enumerate(\n                zip(losses, learning_rates, strict=True)\n            ):\n                handle.write(\n                    json.dumps({\"step\": step, \"loss\": loss, \"lr\": lr}) + \"\\n\"\n                )\n        (run_dir / \"DONE\").touch()\n        return run_dir\n\n    with (run_dir / \"metrics.jsonl\").open(\"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as handle:\n        def record(step: int, loss: float, lr: float) -> None:\n            handle.write(json.dumps({\"step\": step, \"loss\": loss, \"lr\": lr}) + \"\\n\")\n            handle.flush()\n\n        model, _ = train_model(config, on_step=record)\n    if config.variant in {\"m1\", \"m1b\"}:\n        assert_stable(model)\n    checkpoint = run_dir / \"final.pt\"\n    torch.save({\"step\": config.steps, \"model\": model.state_dict()}, checkpoint)\n    from stencil.evaluate import evaluate_model  # Avoid an entrypoint cycle.\n\n    result = evaluate_model(model, config)\n    (run_dir / \"eval.json\").write_bytes(canonical_json(result) + b\"\\n\")\n    (run_dir / \"DONE\").touch()\n    return run_dir\n\n\ndef _prepare_run_dir(\n    run_dir: Path, identity: GitIdentity, force: bool\n) -> None:\n    if run_dir.exists():\n        if not force:\n            raise FileExistsError(f\"run directory already exists: {run_dir}\")\n        env_path = run_dir / \"env.json\"\n        try:\n            prior = json.loads(env_path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n        except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:\n\"\"\"Shared base transformer and Phase 2 model-variant assembly.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections import OrderedDict\n\nimport torch\nfrom torch import nn\nfrom torch.nn import functional as F\n\nfrom stencil.config import Config\nfrom stencil.determinism import named_generator\nfrom stencil.gates import apply_headwise_gate, project_b1_gate, project_control_gate\nfrom stencil.oscillator import CueLatch, DecayCell, OscillatorController\n\n\nclass Attention(nn.Module):\n    def __init__(self, config: Config, layer_index: int) -> None:\n        super().__init__()\n        self.d_model = config.d_model\n        self.n_heads = config.n_heads\n        if config.d_model % config.n_heads:\n            raise ValueError(\"d_model must be divisible by n_heads\")\n        self.head_dim = config.d_model // config.n_heads\n        if self.head_dim % 2:\n            raise ValueError(\"RoPE head dimension must be even\")\n        self.window = None if config.variant == \"b0_full\" else config.window\n        self._use_banded = self.window is not None\n        self._banded_block_size = None if self.window is None else 8 * self.window\n        self.rope_theta = config.rope_theta\n        self.layer_index = layer_index\n        self.q = nn.Linear(config.d_model, config.d_model, bias=False)\n        self.k = nn.Linear(config.d_model, config.d_model, bias=False)\n        self.v = nn.Linear(config.d_model, config.d_model, bias=False)\n        self.o = nn.Linear(config.d_model, config.d_model, bias=False)\n\n    def _rope(self, value: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:\n        length = value.shape[2]\n        frequency = self.rope_theta ** (\n            -torch.arange(0, self.head_dim, 2, device=value.device, dtype=value.dtype)\n            / self.head_dim\n        )\n        angle = (\n            torch.arange(length, device=value.device, dtype=value.dtype)[:, None]\n            * frequency[None]\n        )\n        cosine = angle.cos()[None, None]\n        sine = angle.sin()[None, None]\n        even, odd = value[..., 0::2], value[..., 1::2]\n        return torch.stack(\n            (even * cosine - odd * sine, even * sine + odd * cosine), dim=-1\n        ).flatten(-2)\n\n    def _banded_layout(\n        self,\n        length: int,\n        cue_mask: torch.Tensor | None,\n        device: torch.device,\n    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:\n        \"\"\"Return gathered key positions and their validity mask.\n\n        Positions within each row are ordered as old global cues followed by\n        the chronological local window.  A cue already in the local window is\n        excluded from the global portion, so every allowed key occurs once.\n        \"\"\"\n        assert self.window is not None\n        queries = torch.arange(length, device=device)\n        local_positions = (\n            queries[:, None] + torch.arange(1 - self.window, 1, device=device)[None]\n        )\n        local_valid = local_positions >= 0\n        local_positions = local_positions.clamp_min(0)\n        if cue_mask is None:\n            return local_positions[None], local_valid[None]\n\n        max_cues = int(cue_mask.sum(dim=1).max().item())\n        if max_cues:\n            all_positions = queries[None].expand(cue_mask.shape[0], -1)\n            global_positions = torch.where(cue_mask, all_positions, length)\n            global_positions = global_positions.sort(dim=1).values[:, :max_cues]\n            global_positions = global_positions[:, None].expand(-1, length, -1)\n            global_valid = global_positions <= queries[None, :, None] - self.window\n            global_positions = global_positions.clamp_max(length - 1)\n        else:\n            global_positions = queries.new_empty(cue_mask.shape[0], length, 0)\n            global_valid = cue_mask.new_empty(cue_mask.shape[0], length, 0)\n        batch = cue_mask.shape[0]\n        return (\n            torch.cat(\n                (global_positions, local_positions[None].expand(batch, -1, -1)),\n                dim=-1,\n            ),\n            torch.cat(\n                (global_valid, local_valid[None].expand(batch, -1, -1)),\n                dim=-1,\n            ),\n        )\n\n    def _forward_banded(\n        self,\n        q: torch.Tensor,\n        k: torch.Tensor,\n        v: torch.Tensor,\n        cue_mask: torch.Tensor | None,\n    ) -> torch.Tensor:\n        \"\"\"Compute exact causal-window attention in O(T * (window + cues)).\"\"\"\n        assert self.window is not None\n        batch, _, length, _ = q.shape\n        queries = torch.arange(length, device=q.device)\n        global_k = None\n        global_v = None\n        global_positions = None\n        if cue_mask is not None:\n            max_cues = int(cue_mask.sum(dim=1).max().item())\n            if max_cues:\n                all_positions = queries[None].expand(batch, -1)\n                global_positions = torch.where(cue_mask, all_positions, length)\n                global_positions = global_positions.sort(dim=1).values[:, :max_cues]\n                gather_positions = global_positions.clamp_max(length - 1)\n                gather_index = gather_positions[:, None, :, None].expand(\n                    -1, self.n_heads, -1, self.head_dim\n                )\n                global_k = torch.gather(k, 2, gather_index)\n                global_v = torch.gather(v, 2, gather_index)\n\n        chunks: list[torch.Tensor] = []\n        assert self._banded_block_size is not None\n        query_block = self._banded_block_size\n        for start in range(0, length, query_block):\n            end = min(start + query_block, length)\n            key_start = max(0, start - self.window + 1)\n            query_positions = queries[start:end]\n            local_positions = queries[key_start:end]\n            lag = query_positions[:, None] - local_positions[None]\n            local_valid = (lag >= 0) & (lag < self.window)\n            block_k = k[:, :, key_start:end]\n            block_v = v[:, :, key_start:end]\n\n            if global_positions is not None:\n                assert global_k is not None and global_v is not None\n                global_valid = (\n                    global_positions[:, None]\n                    <= query_positions[None, :, None] - self.window\n                )\n                valid = torch.cat(\n                    (\n                        global_valid,\n                        local_valid[None].expand(batch, -1, -1),\n                    ),\n                    dim=-1,\n                )\n                block_k = torch.cat((global_k, block_k), dim=2)\n                block_v = torch.cat((global_v, block_v), dim=2)\n            else:\n                valid = local_valid\n\n            chunks.append(\n                F.scaled_dot_product_attention(\n                    q[:, :, start:end],\n                    block_k,\n                    block_v,\n                    attn_mask=valid[:, None] if valid.ndim == 3 else valid,\n                )\n            )\n        return torch.cat(chunks, dim=2)\n\n    def forward(\n        self,\n        x: torch.Tensor,\n        gates: torch.Tensor | None,\n        cue_mask: torch.Tensor | None = None,\n        *,\n        use_banded: bool | None = None,\n    ) -> torch.Tensor:\n        batch, length, _ = x.shape\n\n        def reshape(value: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:\n            return value.view(batch, length, self.n_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(\n                1, 2\n            )\n\n        q = self._rope(reshape(self.q(x)))\n        k = self._rope(reshape(self.k(x)))\n        v = reshape(self.v(x))\n        if cue_mask is not None and (\n None:\n            use_banded = self._use_banded\n        if use_banded and self.window is not None:\n            heads = self._forward_banded(q, k, v, cue_mask)\n        else:\n            positions = torch.arange(length, device=x.device)\n            lag = positions[:, None] - positions[None, :]\n            mask = lag >= 0\n            if self.window is not None:\n                local = lag < self.window\n                if cue_mask is not None:\n                    if (\n                        cue_mask.shape != (batch, length)\n                        or cue_mask.dtype != torch.bool\n                    ):\n                        raise ValueError(\n                            \"cue_mask must be boolean with shape (batch, length)\"\n                        )\n                    mask = mask[None, None] & (\n                        local[None, None] | cue_mask[:, None, None, :]\n                    )\n                else:\n                    mask = mask & local\n            heads = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, attn_mask=mask)\n        if gates is not None:\n            heads = apply_headwise_gate(heads, gates)\n        merged = heads.transpose(1, 2).contiguous().view(batch, length, self.d_model)\n        return self.o(merged)\n\n\nclass Block(nn.Module):\n    def __init__(self, config: Config, layer_index: int) -> None:\n        super().__init__()\n        self.attention_norm = nn.LayerNorm(config.d_model, eps=1e-5)\n        self.attention = Attention(config, layer_index)\n        self.mlp_norm = nn.LayerNorm(config.d_model, eps=1e-5)\n        self.up = nn.Linear(config.d_model, config.d_ff, bias=False)\n        self.down = nn.Linear(config.d_ff, config.d_model, bias=False)\n\n    def forward(\n        self,\n        x:    x = x + self.down(F.gelu(self.up(self.mlp_norm(x))))\n        return x\n\n\nclass StencilTransformer(nn.Module):\n    \"\"\"One shared decoder-only transformer assembled into all eight variants.\"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, config: Config) -> None:\n        super().__init__()\n        if config.variant not in {\n            \"b0_full\",\n            \"b0_local\",\n            \"b1\",\n            \"b2\",\n            \"m1\",\n            \"m1b\",\n            \"b3\",\n            \"b4\",\n        }:\n            raise ValueError(\"unknown model variant\")\n        self.config = config\n        self.token_embedding = nn.Embedding(config.vocab, config.d_model)\n        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList(\n            [Block(config, index) for index in range(config.n_layers)]\n        )\n        self.final_norm = nn.LayerNorm(config.d_model, eps=1e-5)\n        self.lm_head = nn.Linear(config.d_model, config.vocab, bias=False)\n\n        generator = named_generator(config.seed_init, \"init\")\n        self._initialize_base(generator)\n        pathway_generator = named_generator(config.seed_init, \"pathway\")\n        self.controller: nn.Module | None = None\n        self.gate_weight: nn.Parameter | None = None\n        self.gate_bias: nn.Parameter | None = None\n        self.b1_weight: nn.Parameter | None = None\n        if config.variant in {\"m1\", \"m1b\"}:\n            self.controller = OscillatorController(config, pathway_generator)\n        elif config.variant == \"b2\":\n            self.controller = DecayCell(\n                config.d_model, 128, generator=pathway_generator\n            )\n        elif config.variant == \"b3\":\n            self.controller = CueLatch(config.d_model, 128, generator=pathway_generator)\n        if config.variant in {\"m1\", \"m1b\", \"b2\", \"b3\"}:\n            self.gate_weight = nn.Parameter(\n                torch.empty(config.n_layers, config.n_heads, 128)\n            )\n            self.gate_bias = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(config.n_layers, config.n_heads))\n            nn.init.normal_(\n                self.gate_weight,\n                mean=0.0,\n                std=1e-3,\n                generator=pathway_generator,\n            )\n        elif config.variant == \"b1\":\n            self.b1_weight = nn.Parameter(\n                torch.empty(config.n_layers, config.n_heads, config.d_model)\n            )\n            nn.init.normal_(\n                self.b1_weight,\n                mean=0.0,\n                std=0.02,\n                generator=pathway_generator,\n            )\n\n    def _initialize_base(self, generator: torch.Generator) -> None:\n        nn.init.normal_(\n            self.token_embedding.weight, mean=0.0, std=0.02, generator=generator\n        )\n        for block in self.blocks:\n            for linear in (\n                block.attention.q,\n                block.attention.k,\n                block.attention.v,\n                block.attention.o,\n                block.up,\n                block.down,\n            ):\n                nn.init.normal_(linear.weight, mean=0.0, std=0.02, generator=generator)\n            nn.init.ones_(block.attention_norm.weight)\n            nn.init.zeros_(block.attention_norm.bias)\n            nn.init.ones_(block.mlp_norm.weight)\n            nn.init.zeros_(block.mlp_norm.bias)\n receptive_field(self) -> int:\n        return self.config.n_layers * (self.config.window - 1)\n\n    def forward(\n        self, tokens: torch.Tensor, *, gate_identity: bool = False\n    ) -> torch.Tensor:\n        return self.forward_embeddings(\n            self.token_embedding(tokens),\n            gate_identity=gate_identity,\n            cue_mask=(tokens >= 1) & (tokens <= 32),\n        )\n\n    def forward_embeddings(\n        self,\n        embeddings: torch.Tensor,\n        *,\n        gate_identity: bool = False,\n        cue_mask: torch.Tensor | None = None,\n    ) -> torch.Tensor:\n        if gate_identity and self.config.variant in {\"b0_full\", \"b0_local\"}:\n            raise ValueError(\"baseline has no gate to bypass\")\n        control = None\n        if self.config.variant == \"b3\":\n            if cue_mask is None:\n                raise ValueError(\"b3 embedding forwards require a cue_mask\")\n            assert isinstance(self.controller, CueLatch)\n            control = self.controller(embeddings, cue_mask)\n        elif self.controller is not None:\n            control = self.controller(embeddings)\n        if self.config.variant == \"b4\" and cue_mask is None:\n            raise ValueError(\"b4 embedding forwards require a cue_mask\")\n        x = embeddings\n        for layer_index, block in enumerate(self.blocks):\n            normalized = block.attention_norm(x)\n            gates = None\n            if self.config.variant == \"b1\":\n                if gate_identity:\n                    gates = x.new_ones(x.shape[0], x.shape[1], self.config.n_heads)\n                else:\n                    assert self.b1_weight is not None\n                    gates = project_b1_gate(normalized, self.b1_weight[layer_index])\n            elif self.gate_weight is not None:\n                if gate_identity:\n                    gates = x.new_ones(x.shape[0], x.shape[1], self.config.n_heads)\n                else:\n                    assert control is not None and self.gate_bias is not None\n                    gates = project_control_gate(\n                        control,\n                        self.gate_weight[layer_index],\n                        self.gate_bias[layer_index],\n                    )\n            attention_cue_mask = cue_mask if self.config.variant == \"b4\" else None\n count_params(module: nn.Module) -> int:\n    return sum(\n        parameter.numel()\n        for parameter in module.parameters()\n        if parameter.requires_grad\n    )\n\n\ndef _config_param_count(config: Config) -> int:\n    d = config.d_model\n    base = (\n        2 * config.vocab * d\n        + config.n_layers * (4 * d * d + 2 * d * config.d_ff + 4 * d)\n        + 2 * d\n    )\n    gates = config.n_layers * config.n_heads * (128 + 1)\n    if config.variant == \"b1\":\n        return base + config.n_layers * config.n_heads * d\n    if config.variant == \"b2\":\n None\n        m = config.osc_pairs\n        pathway = m * d + 3 * m * m + 2 * m + gates\n        if config.variant == \"m1b\":\n            pathway += 2 * m\n        return base + pathway\n    return base\n\n\ndef _base_config(variant: str, d_ff: int, seed_init: int) -> Config:\n    oscillatory = variant in {\"m1\", \"m1b\"}\n    return Config(\n        seed_data=0,\n        seed_init=seed_init,\n        seed_train=0,\n        variant=variant,\n        d_model=256,\n        n_layers=4,\n        n_heads=4,\n        d_ff=d_ff,\n        window=64,\n        vocab=64,\n        context_len=2052,\n        rope_theta=10_000.0,\n        osc_pairs=64 if oscillatory else None,\n        osc_cells=2 if oscillatory else None,\n        period_min=8.0 if oscillatory else None,\n        period_max=4096.0 if oscillatory else None,\n        damping_learnable=(variant == \"m1b\") if oscillatory else None,\n        task=\"a\",\n        seed_rules=0,\n        task_N=2048,\n        task_k=8,\n        task_R=None,\n        task_delay_min=None,\n        task_delay_max=None,\n        task_P=None,\n        task_queries=None,\n        task_placement=None,\n\"\"\"Oscillator and decay control pathways plus their sequential proof helpers.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport math\n\nimport torch\nfrom torch import nn\nfrom torch.nn import functional as F\n\nfrom stencil.config import Config\n\n_SCAN_BLOCK_SIZE = 256\n\n\ndef _inverse_softplus(value: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:\n    return value + torch.log(-torch.expm1(-value))\n\n\ndef discrete_invariant(\n    y: torch.Tensor,\n    z: torch.Tensor,\n    a: torch.Tensor,\n    dt: float = 1.0,\n) -> torch.Tensor:\n    \"\"\"Return symplectic Euler's exactly conserved modified energy.\n\n    Substitution of ``z' = z-dt*A*y`` and ``y' = y+dt*z'`` into this\n    quadratic cancels every term, giving H_d' = H_d when forcing and damping\n    are zero: H_d = z^2 + A*y^2 - dt*A*y*z.\n    \"\"\"\n    return z.square() + a * y.square() - dt * a * y * z\n\n\ndef _interleave_scan_parts(\n    first: torch.Tensor,\n    odd: torch.Tensor,\n    even: torch.Tensor,\n    length: int,\n) -> torch.Tensor:\n    \"\"\"Interleave recursive scan results along dimension one.\"\"\"\n    if length % 2:\n        tail = torch.stack((odd, even), dim=2).flatten(1, 2)\n    else:\n        paired = torch.stack((odd[:, :-1], even), dim=2).flatten(1, 2)\n        tail = torch.cat((paired, odd[:, -1:]), dim=1)\n    return torch.cat((first[:, :1], tail), dim=1)\n\n\ndef _scan_affine_2x2(\n    transform: tuple[torch.Tensor, ...],\n) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, ...]:\n    \"\"\"Inclusive fixed-tree scan of per-mode two-dimensional affine maps.\"\"\"\n    length = transform[0].shape[1]\n    if length < 2:\n        return transform\n\n    left = tuple(value[:, 0:-1:2] for value in transform)\n    right = tuple(value[:, 1::2] for value in transform)\n    l00, l01, l10, l11, ld0, ld1 = left\n    r00, r01, r10, r11, rd0, rd1 = right\n    reduced = _scan_affine_2x2(\n        (\n            r00 * l00 + r01 * l10,\n            r00 * l01 + r01 * l11,\n            r10 * l00 + r11 * l10,\n            r10 * l01 + r11 * l11,\n            r00 * ld0 + r01 * ld1 + rd0,\n            r10 * ld0 + r11 * ld1 + rd1,\n        )\n    )\n\n    even_source = tuple(value[:, 2::2] for value in transform)\n    prefix = reduced if length % 2 else tuple(value[:, :-1] for value in reduced)\n    l00, l01, l10, l11, ld0, ld1 = prefix\n    r00, r01, r10, r11, rd0, rd1 = even_source\n    even = (\n        r00 * l00 + r01 * Determinism contract\n\nEvery training or eval entrypoint must satisfy the following.\n\n- Single source of randomness. One `torch.Generator` per named stream, seeded deterministically from the config (v1.7): stream `name` under seed `s` uses `int.from_bytes(sha256(f\"{s}:{name}\".encode()).digest()[:8], \"big\") >> 1`. Registered stream names: `init`, `train`, and per-task `rules`, `cues`, `operands`, `distractors`, `keys`, `values`, `queries`, `delays`. This scheme is part of the contract so fixtures can be hand-executed. Dropout is disabled entirely in v1.\n- Experiment-seed mapping (v1.7): \"seeds {0, 1, 2}\" in any matrix means experiment seed `s` sets `seed_init = seed_train = seed_data = s`, with `seed_rules = 0` for every Phase 3-5 run (one rule table per cell across seeds, a task property, not a robustness axis).\n- `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` and `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8` set in a shared `determinism.py` imported by every entrypoint.\n- fp32 for all toy-phase training. Model-level proof tests (Phase 2 tests 6-8 and their reruns) execute models in fp32. Cell-numerics tests (Phase 2 tests 1-2) may execute the isolated cell in fp64 where their registered cases say so, alongside the registered fp32-vs-fp64 consistency bound (scoped v1.8, reconciled v1.12). Test-side references may always use fp64. bf16 is permitted only in Phase 6 training and never in proof tests.\n- Every run writes `results/<run_id>/config.json`, `metrics.jsonl`, and `env.json` (git SHA, torch version, GPU name, driver). `run_id` = first 12 hex chars of `sha256(canonical_json(config) + git_sha + sha256(git diff HEAD) + sha256(untracked_record))` where `untracked_record` concatenates, in sorted path order, one `(utf8_path, NUL, decimal_length, NUL, content)` record per untracked non-ignored file (framed v1.11 — renames and content repartitions cannot collide). Byte contract, complete (v1.13): every sha256 in this formula is rendered as ASCII lowercase hex (64 chars); `git_sha` is the 40-char lowercase hex ASCII string; the outer preimage is the UTF-8 bytes of `canonical_json`, then `git_sha`, then `hex(sha256(git diff HEAD bytes))`, then `hex(sha256(untracked_record))`, concatenated in that order with no separators; `run_id` is the first 12 hex chars of the outer digest. `env.json` records the two inner hex digests alongside the git SHA (v1.7/v1.10/v1.11; no dirty or untracked state can collide with clean evidence). Runs that feed a gate must start from a clean worktree; a dirty-tree run requires `--allow-dirty`, is stamped `dirty` in `env.json`, and is ineligible as gate evidence. `--force` refuses to delete an existing run directory whose `env.json` records a different git state — such a directory is removed only by hand. Matrix resume contract (v1.7): a run writes a `DONE` marker file after its final eval; `run_matrix.py` skips cells whose directory carries `DONE`, and restarts (recreating the directory) cells that were interrupted mid-run with identical config and git state.\n- `scripts/verify_determinism.py` trains seed 0 for 200 steps twice in-process and asserts the loss sequences are bitwise identical. Runs in CI (`make verify`) and as a pytest marker `@pytest.mark.determinism`.\n\nHardware note. Bitwise reproducibility is guaranteed same-machine same-config. The target machine is a DGX Spark (GB10, aarch64, 128 GB unified memory). All toy runs are single-device fp32 and fit trivially.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Repo layout and stack\n\n```\nstencil/\n  PLAN.md                  # this file, governs\n  README.md                # plain-language explanation, component map, gate status table, explains\n  Makefile                 # gate targets: make gate-0 .. gate-4 and gate-6 run that gate's tests/checks;\n                           #   no gate-5 (Phase 5 and 7 exit on reviewed artifacts); make verify = determinism\n  pyproject.toml           # uv-managed, deps: torch, pytest, ruff, numpy, matplotlib\n  src/stencil/\n    determinism.py\n    data.py                # task generators (Task A, Task B, Task M)\n    oscillator.py          # unified damped-oscillator cell, decay cell, sequential oracle + scan impl\n    gates.py               # gate projection and application, incl. Qwen G1 headwise for B1\n    model.py               # base transformer, variant assembly\n    train.py               # single-run trainer\n    evaluate.py            # exact-match eval at answer positions\n    probes.py              # linear probes on control state and on gate vectors\n    patching.py            # control-state causal interventions\n  scripts/\n    run_matrix.py          # runs the full model x seed x task grid from configs\n    make_report.py         # aggregates metrics.jsonl into results/summary.md tables\n    verify_determinism.py\n    gen_jax_fixtures.py    # one-time oracle fixture generation, see Appendix G\n  AGENTS.md                # agent playbook: retro lessons every agent loads (codex natively, Claude via CLAUDE.md)\n  CLAUDE.md                # thin pointer: @AGENTS.md + PLAN.md governance line\n  tools/                   # codex wrappers (Section 2b): run_codex_agent.sh, run_codex_review.sh,\n                           #   run_kimi_review.py, agent_metrics.py, check_review_scores.py,\n                           #   review_*.py, codex-prompts/, codex-agents/\n  plan/                    # the plan's working directory (v1.17)\n    PROTOCOL.md            # Section 2b: roles, review/lens/session rules, autonomy, retros, evals\n    LEDGER.md              # work log + STATE line (operational state; restart from here)\n    AMENDMENTS.md          # full amendment-history prose (PLAN.md keeps the one-line index)\n    reviews/               # canonical adversarial review files, <phase>/<topic>.md (+ <topic>-kimi.md);\n                           #   .sessions/ holds machine-local reviewer thread ids (gitignored)\n    retros/                # phase retrospectives, <phase>.md\n    tiebreaks/             # tie-break prompts and verdicts, <phase>.md\n  configs/                 # one json per cell of the experiment matrix\n  tests/\n    fixtures/              # committed npz reference trajectories from JAX oracles\n  results/                 # gitignored except *.md at its root (summary.md, tradeoff.md, mechanism.md,\n                           #   REPORT.md, POSTMORTEM.md, data_samples.md, params.md) and results/figures/\n```\n\nREADME.md is a governed artifact, provided alongside this plan. Material changes to hypotheses, variants, tasks, or gates require a matching update to its mapping table in the same commit, and every green gate flips its status table row per rule 5. If the two files ever disagree, this file wins and README.md has a bug.\n\nStack decisions, fixed. Plain PyTorch, no Lightning, no Hydra. Configs are flat JSON loaded into a frozen dataclass. `uv` for env, `pytest` for tests, `ruff` for lint. No wandb in v1, metrics are JSONL plus generated markdown tables. Sliding-window masking via plain SDPA with an explicit boolean mask, which is the deterministic default. FlexAttention or other kernels are out of scope for v1.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Architecture spec\n\n### 5.1 Base transformer (shared by all variants)\n\n| item | value |\n|---|---|\n| type | decoder-only, pre-LN, causal |\n| d_model | 256 |\n| layers L | 4 |\n| heads H | 4 (head_dim 64) |\n| d_ff | 1024 (adjusted per variant for param matching, see 5.5) |\n| positional | RoPE |\n| attention | causal sliding window, w = 64 (B0-full uses full causal) |\n| dropout | none |\n| vocab | 64 synthetic tokens (see task spec) |\n| params | ~3.2M |\n\nThe exact attention receptive field after L layers is `L * (w - 1) = 252` positions of maximal lag (v1.6); `L * w = 256` is the conservative bound used when placing unreachable cues. These numbers are load-bearing. `model.receptive_field()` returns `L * (w - 1)`; recompute in code and use it in tests, never hardcode 252 or 256 in tests.\n\nBase-model details, all fixed (v1.6): MLP is GELU with no biases anywhere (attention QKVO and MLP); pre-LN LayerNorm plus a final LayerNorm, eps 1e-5; embedding and LM head untied; rope_theta 10000; every weight initialized N(0, 0.02) with the seeded init generator; no dropout anywhere.\n\n### 5.2 Control pathway (M1 and M1b, unified cell)\n\nA stack of oscillatory state-space cells running left-to-right over the token embeddings, independent of the transformer's residual stream. Independence is deliberate. The control state is then a deterministic function of the input sequence alone, which makes causal patching in Phase 4 clean.\n\nContinuous system per cell, diagonal `A >= 0`, diagonal damping `G >= 0`, input `u_t` = token embedding (256):\n\n```\ny'(t) = z(t)\nz'(t) = -A y(t) - G z(t) + B u(t)\n```\n\nDiscretization is symplectic in the conservative part with the damping treated implicitly, so `G = 0` recovers the conservative IMEX update through the identical code path:\n\n```\nz_{k+1} = ( z_k + dt * (-A y_k + B u_k) ) / (1 + dt * G)\ny_{k+1} = y_k + dt * z_{k+1}\n```\n\nNumerical facts, registered so the tests are honest (v1.4). This update is symplectic Euler with implicit damping. With `G = 0` it does NOT conserve the continuous energy `H = z^2 + A y^2` — at `dt = 1` and period 8 the per-step excursion of `H` is tens of percent — it exactly conserves a modified discrete quadratic invariant (for symplectic Euler on `y'' = -A y`, the shifted energy `H_d = z^2 + A y^2 - dt * A * y * z`; derive and verify the exact form for this code path during implementation and record it in a code comment). \"Conservative\" throughout this plan means: the discrete invariant is exactly conserved, hence trajectories are bounded for all time and nothing is forgotten; it does not mean pointwise conservation of the continuous `H`. Stability requires `dt * sqrt(A) < 2`; period_min = 8 gives `dt * sqrt(A) = 2 * pi / 8 ~ 0.785`, satisfied with margin, and `A` is re-checked against the bound after training. Closed-form comparisons in tests use the exact discrete solution (matrix power of the one-step map in fp64), not the continuous solution.\n\nVerify both the undamped and damped forms against the LinOSS (arXiv 2410.03943) and D-LinOSS (arXiv 2505.12171) equations during implementation. If they differ materially, record the discrepancy and the chosen resolution as a review-gated amendment (Autonomy policy) — external code never silently overrides the governing equations. Cross-check numerically against committed JAX fixtures per Appendix G (pinned commits and versions listed there).\n\nTensor shapes, fixed (v1.4). Cell 1: `B_1 in R^{64 x 256}` reads token embeddings; states `y_1, z_1 in R^64`, initialized to zeros. Between cells: GLU `u_2 = (W_a y_1) * sigmoid(W_b y_1)` with `W_a, W_b in R^{64 x 64}`. Cell 2: `B_2 in R^{64 x 64}` reads `u_2`; states `y_2, z_2 in R^64`, zeros init. The control output is `c_t = [y_2 ; z_2] in R^128` — the final cell's full state, no extra readout (the \"readout\" is the gate projection in 5.3). Phase 4's probed and patched object `c` is exactly this `c_t`. Per-cell parameters `a_raw, g_raw in R^64`. No biases on `B_i`, `W_a`, `W_b`.\n\n| item | value |\n|---|---|\n| oscillator pairs m | 64 (state dim 128: y and z each 64) |\n## Phase 0. Scaffold and determinism harness\n\nObjective. Empty repo to green determinism gate.\n\nTests first:\n- `test_determinism_two_runs_bitwise`. Uses the committed `configs/test_tiny.json`, registered in full (v1.11): variant b0_local, d_model 64, L 2, H 2, d_ff 256, w 16, vocab 64, task `copy` — sequences of 64 tokens uniform over the operand range from the `operands` stream, target at each position = previous token, loss over positions 1 onward — batch 8, 200 steps, the Phase 3 optimizer block, fp32, all seeds 0, single device; trains twice in-process from identical seeds and asserts the two 200-entry loss sequences are bitwise identical.\n- `test_config_hash_stable`. Config hashing is `sha256` of the canonical JSON encoding — keys sorted, separators `(\",\", \":\")`, floats via `repr` — of the full config dict, `run_id` per the Section 3 formula verbatim (the four-term v1.11 form with the framed untracked record; Section 3 is the sole authority and this sentence intentionally does not restate it). Test asserts key-order independence and a registered known answer (v1.6): `canonical_json({\"b\": 2, \"a\": 1.5})` must be the bytes `{\"a\":1.5,\"b\":2}` and its sha256 must equal the value the orchestrator computes by hand with `python3 -c` and records in the test file before the hashing code exists (TDD-conform).\n- `test_seed_isolation`. Changing `seed_data` leaves the initial `state_dict` bytes identical and changes the first batch's token tensor; changing `seed_init` does the reverse.\n\nRun-directory policy (v1.4): `results/<run_id>/` is created fresh per run; if it already exists the trainer refuses to start unless `--force` is passed, and `--force` deletes and recreates the directory ONLY when its `env.json` records the same git state (aligned v1.9 with Section 3 — evidence from different code is never deleted by tooling). Metrics are never appended across invocations.\n\nTasks: repo layout, place the provided README.md at the repo root with every status row set to not started, `determinism.py`, config dataclass + hashing (the loader validates: unknown fields rejected, `damping_learnable` must be consistent with `variant`, task fields required iff the task uses them), minimal train loop on a dummy copy task, Makefile with `verify` and `gate-0`.\n\nGate G0: `make gate-0` runs the three tests plus ruff. Exit: green, commit.\n\n## Phase 1. Data generators\n\nTests first:\n- `test_task_a_exact_output` (fixed seed, assert exact token sequences against committed fixture files for k=2, N=8 miniatures; TDD-conform protocol registered v1.6: the orchestrator hand-executes the registered constructions — cyclic-square sampler, sampling semantics, alignment contract — for `seed_rules=0, seed_data=0`, writes the expected sequences into the fixture BEFORE the generator is implemented, and the generator must then reproduce them exactly; any mismatch is adjudicated against the registered construction, never by regenerating the fixture)\n- `test_rules_are_permutations` (bijectivity per rule)\n- `test_vocab_ranges_disjoint`\n- `test_distractor_rule_independence` (frequency check described in Section 6: resample the rule assignment 10,000 times with distractors held fixed, assert each rule's frequency within 5 sigma of uniform)\n- `test_rules_latin_rectangle` (for each dataset seed tested: every row a permutation, every column of the k x 16 output table has distinct entries for k <= 16 and exactly-two-per-answer balance for k = 32, and `cue_blind_bayes(config)` returns exactly 1/k or 1/16 accordingly)\n- `test_loss_mask_positions` (mask true exactly at answer-DECISION positions — the input positions whose logits predict answer tokens, per the Section 6 contract — all three tasks; wording corrected v1.6)\n- `test_task_b_active_rule_tracking` (metadata's active-rule labels match most-recent-cue semantics on constructed cases)\n- `test_task_m_bindings` (keys unique within a sequence, every query key appeared as a pair, answers match the binding; exact miniature fixture at P = 4 with 2 queries, `seed_rules = 0, seed_data = 0`, 4 sequences, authored under the same fixture-before-generator protocol as Task A; draw order per sequence: key permutation via one `randperm` on `keys`, P value `randint`s on `values`, query subset via one `randperm` on `queries` taking the first entries, v1.11)\n- `test_task_m_gap_exceeds_receptive_field` (beyond-window placement's minimum pair-to-query distance strictly greater than `receptive_field()` from the model config it will be paired with)\n\nGate G1: all data tests green, plus a generated `results/data_samples.md` showing 3 decoded samples per task and placement for human eyeball. The Phase 1 review MUST include the reviewer's own hand-verification of the committed fixtures against the registered constructions, recorded in the review file (binding condition of the 2026-08-22 tie-break on spec#9, plan/tiebreaks/plan.md). Exit: green, commit.\n\n## Phase 2. Models and plumbing proofs\n\nTests first, in this order:\n\n1. `test_oscillator_matches_discrete_closed_form` (v1.4; cases registered v1.8; numerics fixed v1.11). Single oscillators at periods {8, 64, 4096}, each under zero forcing (initial state `y_0, z_0 ~ N(0,1)` from stream `fixtures:init`, nonzero by construction) and unit constant forcing (b = 1, u = 1, `y_0 = z_0 = 0`), G in {0, 1e-2}: the cell executed in fp64 must match the exact discrete solution (matrix power of the one-step map plus the forced particular solution, fp64) over 1000 steps at rtol 1e-9, atol 1e-12 — the old absolute 1e-5 was infeasible: unit forcing at period 4096 reaches ~4e5 amplitude, where fp32 ulps are ~3e-2. Separately, the fp32 cell must match the fp64 cell at rtol 1e-4, atol 1e-6 on the same cases (this pair, not the closed form, bounds production numerics). Every tolerance in Phase 2 is rtol/atol, stated explicitly. A separate non-gating analysis records the discrete-vs-continuous deviation versus dt for the report.\n2. `test_discrete_invariant_conserved` (v1.4, fixtures instantiated v1.6, completed v1.13). Zero input, `y, z ~ N(0,1)` from stream `fixtures:init` seed 0, standard log-spaced `A`, G = 0: the registered discrete invariant `H_d` (Section 5.2) drifts less than rtol 1e-5 in fp64 and rtol 1e-3 in fp32 over 10k steps, and the continuous energy `H = z^2 + A y^2` stays bounded — max excursion below 4x its initial value — with no trend: window = 1000 steps, trend = least-squares slope over the last five window means, |slope| < 1e-6 x `H_0` per window (v1.13). `test_damped_energy_decays`, two registered G regimes (v1.6): (a) G = 1e-2 fixed: windowed 1k-step means strictly decreasing and `H_10000 < 1e-2 * H_0`; (b) G = softplus(-9) ~ 1.23e-4 (the registered M1b init): windowed means non-increasing and the `H_10000 / H_0` ratio within [0.8, 1.2] x `(1+G)^(-10000)` (~0.29; exponent corrected v1.7 — the v1.6 formula double-counted the per-step determinant; verify the exact modal decay analytically during implementation and record it in a code comment). `test_decay_ssm_energy_decays` for B2's cell: state dim 128, λ = 0.999, initial state N(0,1) from `fixtures:init` seed 0, zero input, 10k steps, windowed means non-increasing and final state-norm-squared ratio within [0.8, 1.2] x `λ^(2 * 10000)` (v1.13).\n2b. `test_stability_bound` (v1.6). Asserts `dt * sqrt(A) < 2` elementwise for every oscillator at init, and provides the checkpoint assertion reused by the gates: every checkpoint entering G3/G4/G6 evidence must pass it (a violation makes that gate red — validity condition in Appendix C).\n3. `test_damping_zero_matches_m1_bitwise`. Instantiate the unified cell as M1b, set the damping to exactly zero through the code path built for M1's frozen buffer (a `zero_damping` flag that bypasses `softplus`, since `softplus(g_raw)` can never be exactly 0 for finite `g_raw`), drive both with N(0,1) inputs (length 512, stream `fixtures:input` seed 0) from N(0,1) initial states (`fixtures:init`), assert outputs are nonzero and bitwise identical to the M1 configuration in fp32 (nonzero-input case registered v1.13 — a zero trajectory would pass vacuously). Guarantees M1 and M1b differ only in dissipation.\n4. `test_cell_matches_jax_fixtures`. Sequential PyTorch cells reproduce the committed reference trajectories from the official JAX implementations at rtol 1e-5, atol 1e-8 (v1.13). Pinned oracles (v1.6): tk-rusch/linoss @ `05a835355439ee5500b2c8f891132c53adf020c0`, jaredbmit/damped-linoss @ `450b546f693918fe7cfe44082e88538fb29fbd64`; `gen_jax_fixtures.py` runs in a throwaway uv env pinned to `jax==0.4.35` (numpy version recorded), checks out exactly these commits, records versions, shapes, seeds, and dtype in the npz metadata, and generates both undamped and damped cases (G = 0, G = 1e-2; `A` from the registered log-spaced period init, m = 64, drawn via stream `fixtures:a`; `B` and GLU weights N(0, 0.02) via streams `fixtures:b` and `fixtures:glu`) on N(0,1) inputs from stream `fixtures:input`, seeds {0, 1}, length 512, fp64 (v1.7; every parameter stream-determined as of v1.10). Workflow per Appendix G.\n5. `test_scan_equals_sequential`. Runs (and gates G2) only if a parallel scan implementation exists in the repo; it must match the sequential oracle at rtol 1e-5, atol 1e-8 on N(0,1) inputs of shape (batch 4, length 512, m 64), fp32, stream `fixtures:input` seed 0 (v1.13). The sequential loop is the oracle forever. (Sequential is acceptable for v1 speed. Scan is an optimization, gated by this test when present.)\n6. `test_gate_identity_recovers_baseline_bitwise`. Build M1 and B0-local from the same seed with shared-submodule init (the base transformer is constructed first from `seed_init` so both variants consume identical RNG streams for shared modules; pathway modules draw from a separate derived generator), force the gate multiplier to exactly 1.0 via a bypass flag (not by driving the sigmoid), and assert forward logits on one Task A batch (batch 8, the (512, 8) cell, `seed_rules = 0, seed_data = 0`, v1.13) are bitwise identical in fp32. Repeat for B1's gate bypassed to 1.0.\n7. `test_cue_unreachable_exact_zero_grad`. B0-local, fp32, untrained models from seeds {0, 1, 2}, the first 3 eval-stream sequences from each unreachable cell (N = 512 and N = 2048; sample count and fixture identity registered v1.13). For every answer-decision position, compute the Jacobian of the full vocab logit vector with respect to the input-embedding activation at the cue position (the activation at that position, not the embedding table row). Assert every entry is exactly zero, and assert the gradient object is a real zero tensor, not `None` (a `None`/detached graph fails the test — it means the path was never connected, which would make the test vacuous). Repeat for B1. Then assert the same Jacobian is nonzero for M1, M1b, and B2 at the same placements. After Phase 3 training, rerun this test on the trained B0-local and B1 checkpoints as a regression guard. This is the load-bearing proof test.\n8. `test_cue_reachable_when_close`. Same machinery with the cue placed so the cue-to-decision distance is exactly `receptive_field()` (reachable by one path): gradient nonzero for B0-local. Guards against a masking bug that silently blinds the model everywhere, and pins the boundary convention.\n9. `test_param_match_within_1pct` across the six variant configs, and generation of `results/params.md` (Section 5.5).\n\nNon-vacuity rule (v1.9, instantiated v1.10): every Phase 2 test restates its registered cases and tolerances from this spec in its docstring, counts the cases it actually executed, and asserts that count equals the registered count; tensors nonempty, autograd graphs connected (a `None` gradient is a test failure, never a pass), assertions executed per registered case and seed — no proof test can pass by silently skipping its subject.\n\nResidual-determinism rule (v1.10, global): any implementation choice this file leaves open defaults to the deterministic lowest-index / lexicographic / first-in-stream option, recorded in the ledger when exercised — no residual choice may depend on iteration order of unordered containers, wall clock, or hardware.\n\nGate G2: tests 1 through 9 plus 2b green (5 when present). Exit: green, commit. These tests are permanent regression guards, never deleted.\n\n## Phase 3. Toy proof runs\n\nTraining config, fixed for all variants: AdamW (betas 0.9/0.95, eps 1e-8, weight_decay 0.1, no decay on biases, norms, or oscillator parameters), lr 3e-4, cosine to 3e-5, warmup 500, 20k steps, batch 64, grad clip 1.0, fp32, seeds {0, 1, 2}. Fresh data every step from the seeded generator (infinite regime, no memorization axis). Eval per the frozen Section 6 protocol.\n\nPilot first (rule/2b budget discipline): before the matrix, run the single cell M1 at (2048, 8) seed 0 to completion, record steps/sec, peak memory, and wall clock in the ledger, project the full matrix, and set per-run timeouts at 4x the projection. Phase budget: 72 GPU-hours; within 2x of that, launch with the projection recorded in the ledger, beyond 2x pause for the human (Autonomy policy).\n\nMatrix:\n- Task A: 6 variants x 3 seeds x cells {(512, 8), (2048, 8), (2048, 32)}, plus the sanity cell (128, 8) for B0-local, M1, M1b, and B2 (extended v1.6 so Appendix D item 2's evidence exists).\n- Task M: variants {B0-full, B0-local, M1, M1b, B2} x 3 seeds x 2 placements.\n- Roughly 90 to 100 runs at ~3M params. Budget expectation is a weekend of Spark time worst case. `run_matrix.py` executes it, `make_report.py` writes `results/summary.md` with mean and min-seed accuracy per cell.\n\nGate G3 (thresholds from Appendix C, evaluated on the summary table; every bar is applied per cell, min-seed bars at each cell separately):\n- G3.1 construction holds: B0-local and B1 at or below the cell's cue-blind null + 2 pts on every unreachable Task A cell (nulls per Section 6: 12.5 for k=8, 6.25 for k=32), and B0-local at or below 8.25 on the beyond-window Task M cell.\n- G3.2 necessity: M1 mean >= 95 at (512, 8) and >= 90 at (2048, 8), min seed >= 85 at each of those cells.\n- G3.2b necessity for M1b: same bars as G3.2.\n- G3.3 sanity: B0-local >= 95 at (128, 8).\n- G3.4 efficiency reference: the primary oscillatory variant within 3 pts of B0-full at (512, 8) (comparator aligned with Appendix C and the outcome procedure, v1.22).\n- G3.5 dissipation spectrum (record-only, no kill): evaluate the H2 decision rule (Section 1) at (2048, 32) and record supported / refuted / inconclusive.\n- G3.6 Task M: B0-full >= 95 on the in-window cell (sanity; a miss triggers diagnosis per Section 6 before proceeding). References to \\\"Section 2b\\\" anywhere in this repo mean this file; \\\"this file\\\" in inherited text means the governed plan (PLAN.md plus this protocol). PLAN.md governs the science; this file governs how agents execute and review it.\\n\\n## 2b. Execution toolchain and adversarial review protocol (added v1.3)\\n\\nRoles, fixed:\\n\\n- Orchestrator: the Claude Code session driving this plan. It decomposes phases into work units, writes briefs, launches sol, verifies review findings, resolves what must be resolved, maintains this file's ledger, and makes gate/commit decisions. It does not write implementation code directly.\\n- Coder: the Codex CLI (`codex exec`) running model `gpt-5.6-sol` at `model_reasoning_effort=medium`, invoked via `tools/run_codex_agent.sh` with a brief in `tools/codex-agents/<name>.md`. Writes all implementation code and tests, following TDD per rule 1.\\n- Reviewer: the same model at `model_reasoning_effort=xhigh`, invoked via `tools/run_codex_review.sh <phase> <topic> <threshold>`. Performs adversarial review of the work, scored 0 to 100, writing to `plan/reviews/<phase>/<topic>.md`.\\n\\nReview protocol:\\n\\n1. Every review is adversarial: the reviewer's job is to break the work, not to bless it. Findings are graded low / medium / high / critical.\\n2. Context carry-over: each review round's prompt includes the prior rounds' full review file verbatim (the wrapper does this), so the reviewer always sees what it previously found, what was claimed fixed, and scores the delta. Round history is append-only in exactly this enforced sense (aligned v1.7): round headings and their recorded Score lines are immutable, high/critical findings may be closed with markers but never vanish, and any other change to prior content MUST carry a dated `(updated ...)` annotation — unannotated silent edits are a protocol violation the next round's reviewer is instructed to flag. `tools/review_round_tracking.py` enforces the mechanical invariants; the annotation duty binds the reviewer.\\n3. Finding identity and closure: a finding's identity is `<topic>#<number>` and its number is stable across rounds. The orchestrator independently verifies every high and critical finding (reads the code, reruns the test, or reproduces the claim), then either fixes it or prepares a refutation with evidence. Closure requires reviewer concurrence: only a subsequent reviewer round may mark a finding `(resolved ...)` or `(refuted ...)` after checking the fix or the refutation evidence itself; the orchestrator never edits reviewer-authored review files. `tools/check_review_scores.py` treats any unmarked high/critical finding as open and fails regardless of score. A human may override a deadlocked finding; the override is recorded in the ledger with rationale.\\n4. Resolution scope: fixes to implementation code and tests go through a coder brief (TDD per rule 1). Every coder brief MUST ship a scope allowlist `tools/codex-agents/<name>.allow` (glob patterns, one per line); the wrapper refuses to launch without one and hard-fails on out-of-scope diffs (mandatory per tie-break batch 2, 2026-08-22). A failed coder run's partial work is preserved as diagnostic evidence, never auto-reverted (same tie-break). Brief contract (v1.13, provenance v1.18): every brief states the objective, the allowlist, the tests to write first, the acceptance command, and the ledger handoff; the handoff entry MUST record the model, effort, wrapper log path, and codex session id actually used, and any CODEX_MODEL/CODEX_EFFORT override requires a ledgered reason. The orchestrator may directly edit only non-implementation files: PLAN.md, the plan/ working directory (PROTOCOL.md, LEDGER.md, AMENDMENTS.md), README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, configs, docs, and process tooling under tools/ (allowlist made explicit for the v1.17 split). Work is accepted only when zero high/critical findings remain open and the review score meets the threshold (default 90). Medium and low findings are recorded in the ledger and may be deferred with a stated reason.\\n5. Cadence: at minimum one review per phase before its exit commit. Lens selection, adaptive (v1.13, human directive): the orchestrator examines the work unit's actual diff and writes a purpose-built rubric fragment `tools/codex-prompts/review-<slug>.md`, where `<slug>` is the review's canonical topic identity: chosen once at first launch, recorded in the write-ahead entry, and reused verbatim for every later round of that review (v1.18) through whatever lens is most likely to break that change (numerical-analysis for cell math, distributional/leakage for generators, equivalence for refactors, claims-vs-evidence for writeups — or several fragments when the diff warrants); the chosen lens and rationale go in the write-ahead ledger entry, and lens adequacy is audited at retros against escaped defects. `review-phase.md` is the fallback when no bespoke lens is warranted, and the phase's kimi cross-review ALWAYS runs the generic `review-phase.md` lens regardless of bespoke sol lenses — the coverage backstop ensuring no diff is reviewed only through orchestrator-chosen lenses (v1.14). Known kimi coverage limits, disclosed rather than implied away (v1.18): kimi sees text artifacts only (no figures/binaries — their absence is stated in its context header) and oversized files are skipped with an explicit marker; amendments use `review-amendment.md`; retros use `review-retro.md` (kimi). Tie-breaks run via `tools/run_tiebreak.py` (prompt committed first, raw response preserved). One review (one canonical file, whatever its lens) still holds one reviewer session across its rounds. Topic manifest (v1.22, closes process#36): each phase's registered reviews live in `plan/reviews/<phase>/topics.txt`, one topic per line, a line reading `<topic> kimi` when a kimi companion (`<topic>-kimi.md`) is required; the manifest is written in the phase's first write-ahead entry and thereafter append-only; both wrappers refuse a topic absent from an existing manifest, and acceptance validates codex files against it and requires every flagged kimi companion. Required gate artifacts may be listed in `plan/reviews/<phase>/artifacts.txt`; the kimi context manifest reports each one present or absent, with byte size and sha256 for PRESENT rows; PRESENT rows for BINARY artifacts must additionally carry a prose description sufficient for content review — hash and size alone do not satisfy presentation — with enforcement binding at the first PRESENT binary row (batch-5 UPHOLD, 2026-08-22). Process #29 is deferred-open until that first row exists, not complete. Plus a review of any change to this file's governed content (hypotheses, thresholds, architecture). Plan-phase acceptance, defined (v1.12): the plan itself is accepted when `tools/check_acceptance.sh plan` passes — all sol plan topics at 90+ with zero open high/critical findings and kimi cross-reviews on file — after which Phase 0 may begin and further plan changes follow the amendment path. The gate's own tests (Appendix C) remain the scientific pass/fail authority; review scores gate code quality and cannot substitute for a green gate, and vice versa.\\n6. Gate acceptance checklist, all items required before a gate commit: (a) gate tests green (or the exact registered qualified state recorded), (b) the phase's sol review accepted, verified by `tools/check_acceptance.sh <phase>` (thresholds hardcoded at 90 inside the script — not parameterizable at invocation, v1.10), (c) the phase's kimi cross-review run before the commit with its confirmed high/critical findings resolved (v1.7), (d) ledger entry written, (e) README status row updated, (f) commit message names the gate state. No item may be waived by the agent.\\n7. The wrappers' file-write policy is mandatory: reviewers write only their canonical review file; coders write only what their brief scopes. Uncontained drift is a hard wrapper failure, not a warning. Wrapper runs are serialized per repo via `.review.lock`; never run a coder and a reviewer concurrently in this repo, and never edit repo files while a wrapper is running (its drift restorer will clobber the edits).\\n8. Budget discipline: before launching any multi-run matrix, run one pilot cell, record measured steps/sec and peak memory in the ledger, derive per-run and total wall-clock estimates, and set each run's timeout to 4x its pilot estimate. A matrix projected within 2x the phase's stated budget may launch with the projection recorded in the ledger; beyond 2x, pause for the human.\\n\\nPurpose-scoped review and stop-loss (v1.23, human ruling — Adjudication 3). THREAT MODEL, registered: agents are trusted-but-fallible; enforcement tooling detects mistakes and is NOT a defense against a malicious same-uid agent (unattainable per batch-2). Every review rubric states its purpose and threat model; findings outside them are out of scope. Stop-loss (round budget, v1.24, human ruling — Adjudication 4): every review has a budget of at most 10 rounds. A review reaching round 10 without acceptance triggers a kimi tie-break on one enumerated question — CONTINUE (further rounds are likely to reach acceptance on the existing findings) or STOP — with the review file's full round history inlined VERBATIM (summaries forbidden, per vacated batch 4) and the prompt committed pre-execution per the tie-break rules. On CONTINUE the budget extends to 15 rounds, an absolute ceiling; on STOP, or on exhausting round 15, the orchestrator decides against the north star (score advisory). Early exit retained from v1.23: ANY review at 3+ rounds with zero open high/criticals is decided by the orchestrator against the north star (score advisory). This supersedes v1.23's one-round cap for tooling-only changes. Budget scope for the canonical amendment topic (v1.25): plan/reviews/plan/amendment.md is a running log across amendment versions; the round budget counts the rounds spent on the amendment version currently under review, starting at 1 for each new version — the file's historical round total does not count against it. The 90-bar remains binding only for phase gates on the science.\\n\\nCross-model review, kimi (v1.6). kimi-k3 (`kimi-k3:cloud` via the local ollama daemon) is the second, independent reviewer: `python3 tools/run_kimi_review.py <phase> <topic> <threshold>` writes `plan/reviews/<phase>/<topic>-kimi.md` under the same round-log, append-only, and severity contracts, serialized on the same lock. Cadence: at least one kimi cross-review per phase on the gate-critical work, plus each retrospective (threshold 75 there). kimi is advisory — sol remains reviewer of record and kimi acceptance is not required for gates — but the orchestrator verifies kimi's high/critical claims and injects confirmed ones into sol's next round for adjudication; a confirmed, unrefuted kimi finding must be resolved like any other. Tie-break: when the orchestrator and sol deadlock on a finding after two full resolve-or-refute round trips, kimi receives the finding text VERBATIM, the fix or refutation evidence, and both arguments verbatim (summaries are forbidden — the vacated batch 4 shows why), and renders a verdict; the verdict is executed and ledger-recorded. Trigger order, reconciled (v1.22): two deadlocked round trips → kimi tie-break; sol disputing an EXECUTED tie-break in its next round → human touchpoint; a second dispute after a human ruling is out of scope for review. Mandatory human touchpoint (1) of the Autonomy policy now triggers only if sol's next round disputes the executed tie-break.\\n\\nReview-session continuity (v1.6). One review (one phase/topic file) is served by ONE reviewer session across all of its rounds: round 1 records the codex thread id (plan/reviews/.sessions/, machine-local, gitignored) and every later round resumes it, so the reviewer keeps its original context and re-verifies its own findings against the diffs instead of re-litigating from scratch. Anti-churn rule, binding on reviewers: rounds after the first re-examine existing findings and the changes; new findings are added only for regressions introduced by fixes or clear in-scope misses from the original review — scope never expands round-over-round. A new review (next phase or topic) starts a fresh session and then holds it for its own rounds. If a stored session is unusable, the wrapper falls back to a fresh run carrying the prior review file, noted in the wrapper log; the orchestrator MUST append the continuity-loss note to plan/LEDGER.md in the same working session (v1.18 — the log alone is not the audit record). kimi is stateless; its continuity is the prior rounds inlined in each call plus the same anti-churn rule.\\n\\nPhase retrospectives and agent evals (v1.6). After each phase's exit commit, before the next phase starts, the orchestrator writes `plan/retros/<phase>.md`: what went well and what went poorly, with evidence (finding counts and severities per round, fix attempts, reruns, wrapper failures, wall clock vs budget), root causes, and concrete optimizations. Every optimization lands as a diff in the retro commit — the AGENTS.md diff is quoted inside the retro document so the kimi retro review audits it (v1.19), an AGENTS.md entry (the agent playbook codex auto-loads and CLAUDE.md imports), a tooling or prompt fix under tools/, or a deferral ledgered with reason; changes to governed content still go through the amendment path. kimi reviews each retro (advisory, threshold 75) against one rubric question: does the retro assign blame where the evidence points. Performance is measured, not self-reported: `tools/agent_metrics.py` computes, from reviewer-authored review files and git history, first-round scores, rounds-to-acceptance, findings-per-round by severity, and open high/critical counts; the retro records the trend plus two hand-counted metrics, escaped defects (a finding whose root cause was accepted in an earlier phase) and lesson recurrence (a new finding matching an existing AGENTS.md lesson — the direct measure of whether the improvement loop works; target zero). Metrics are advisory and never gate science.\\n\\nAutonomy policy (v1.5). The project runs autonomously by default; honesty is enforced by the adversarial review protocol above and by the deterministic proof tests, not by human checkpoints. Concretely: wherever this plan says an amendment or decision is \\\"human-authorized,\\\" the autonomous path is that the orchestrator drafts the amendment with rationale, a sol@xhigh review of it is run (topic `amendment`, same wrapper), and it takes effect only once that review is accepted with zero open high/critical findings; the ledger records it and the human can audit asynchronously. Threshold freezes at first run launch remain absolute — no review can undo a freeze. Freeze scope, clarified by human ruling (Adjudication 5, v1.26): the freeze protects against evidence-driven rescue; a registered constant proven MATHEMATICALLY UNPASSABLE by init-time deterministic evidence alone may be repaired by amendment, and only with an infeasibility proof (measurement plus derivation) recorded in the amendment entry while zero training data exists that the change could rescue. Once any training run exists whose outcome the constant governs, this exception is closed for that constant. Sequencing, auditable (v1.7, binding without exception since the v1.16 human ruling): an amendment's review must be accepted BEFORE the amendment commit lands — the reviewer reads the working-tree diff or draft, which the wrappers support (pre-existing dirty state is baseline, not drift); non-governed narrow commits (tie-break prompts, artifacts) go through `tools/commit_narrow.sh`, which stages only listed paths and refuses governed ones (v1.22, finding #12); amendment commits are made ONLY through `tools/amend.sh`, which takes the repo lock and refuses to commit unless the amendment review is ACCEPTED with its latest round quoting the current tree id from `tools/amend.sh --tree-id` (content binding: the reviewed tree IS the committed tree; any post-review edit changes the id and blocks the commit) and naming this version, the PLAN.md index line and plan/AMENDMENTS.md entry exist, and the topmost STATE line declares this amendment lands in this commit while naming the POST-commit next command (declared intent, v1.21 — committed STATE is fresh by construction) (v1.19, hardened v1.20 after the reviewer found the first version validated none of the review chain). Correction on the record (v1.20): Human Adjudication 2 made pre-commit review binding from that ruling forward; the orchestrator wrongly applied an extinguished initial-loop exception to v1.18 and v1.19 — both stand as committed, their substance reviewed post-hoc by rounds 16-17, and the violation is ledgered. Changes to acceptance tooling (check_review_scores.py, review_round_tracking.py, the wrappers), to reviewer/coder prompt fragments, or to AGENTS.md (behavioral instructions every agent loads; added v1.22 closing process#31) arising from retrospectives likewise take effect only after an amendment review accepts them (fragments added v1.13). Tie-break auditability (v1.13): every future tie-break's full prompt is committed verbatim to plan/tiebreaks/<phase>.md BEFORE the call executes. Ambiguities in this spec (old rule 7) are resolved autonomously by choosing the most conservative reading, recording the choice in the ledger, and flagging it for the next review round, rather than blocking on the human. The only mandatory human touchpoints are: (1) a review finding deadlocked after two full resolve-or-refute round trips, (2) a gate still red after three fix attempts (rule 4), (3) projected spend beyond 2x a phase budget, (4) renting external compute or any spending beyond this machine (Phase 7), and (5) anything destructive or outward-facing. Models and plumbing proofs\\n\\nTests first, in this order:\\n\\n1. `test_oscillator_matches_discrete_closed_form` (v1.4; cases registered v1.8; numerics fixed v1.11). Single oscillators at periods {8, 64, 4096}, each under zero forcing (initial state `y_0, z_0 ~ N(0,1)` from stream `fixtures:init`, nonzero by construction) and unit constant forcing (b = 1, u = 1, `y_0 = z_0 = 0`), G in {0, 1e-2}: the cell executed in fp64 must match the exact discrete solution (matrix power of the one-step map plus the forced particular solution, fp64) over 1000 steps at rtol 1e-9, atol 1e-12 — the old absolute 1e-5 was infeasible: unit forcing at period 4096 reaches ~4e5 amplitude, where fp32 ulps are ~3e-2. Separately, the fp32 cell must match the fp64 cell at rtol 1e-4 with per-case atol = 1e-4 x max|fp64 reference| over that case's trajectory (v1.26 — the v1.8 flat atol 1e-6 was infeasible: fp32 error accumulates to ~n x eps ~ 1.2e-4 of trajectory scale over 1000 steps, and near zero crossings rtol cannot absorb it; measured max amplitude-relative deviation across the 12 registered cases is 2.9e-5, so the corrected bound holds with >=3.4x margin) (this pair, not the closed form, bounds production numerics). Every tolerance in Phase 2 is rtol/atol, stated explicitly. A separate non-gating analysis records the discrete-vs-continuous deviation versus dt for the report.\\n2. `test_discrete_invariant_conserved` (v1.4, fixtures instantiated v1.6, completed v1.13). Zero input, `y, z ~ N(0,1)` from stream `fixtures:init` seed 0, standard log-spaced `A`, G = 0: the registered discrete invariant `H_d` (Section 5.2) drifts less than rtol 1e-5 in fp64 and rtol 1e-3 in fp32 over 10k steps, and the continuous energy `H = z^2 + A y^2` stays bounded — max excursion below 4x its initial value — with no trend: window = 1000 steps, trend = least-squares slope over the last five window means, |slope| < 1e-4 x `H_0` per window (v1.26 — the v1.13 bound 1e-6 was infeasible: the registered log-spaced `A` includes the period-4096 mode, which a 1000-step window undersamples, so window means inherit that mode's own oscillation as apparent trend; measured slope 1.4e-5 x `H_0` with the exact `H_d` conserved to registered drift bounds, which — with the 4x excursion cap — carry the actual conservation proof; the corrected bound holds with ~7x margin). `test_damped_energy_decays`, two registered G regimes (v1.6): (a) G = 1e-2 fixed: windowed 1k-step means strictly decreasing and `H_10000 < 1e-2 * H_0`; (b) G = softplus(-9) ~ 1.23e-4 (the registered M1b init): windowed means non-increasing and the `H_10000 / H_0` ratio within [0.8, 1.2] x `(1+G)^(-10000)` (~0.29; exponent corrected v1.7 — the v1.6 formula double-counted the per-step determinant; verify the exact modal decay analytically during implementation and record it in a code comment). `test_decay_ssm_energy_decays` for B2's cell: state dim 128, λ = 0.999, initial state N(0,1) from `fixtures:init` seed 0, zero input, 10k steps, windowed means non-increasing and final state-norm-squared ratio within [0.8, 1.2] x `λ^(2 * 10000)` (v1.13).\\n2b. `test_stability_bound` (v1.6). Asserts `dt * sqrt(A) < 2` elementwise for every oscillator at init, and provides the checkpoint assertion reused by the gates: every checkpoint entering G3/G4/G6 evidence must pass it (a violation makes that gate red — validity condition in Appendix C).\\n3. `test_damping_zero_matches_m1_bitwise`. Instantiate the unified cell as M1b, set the damping to exactly zero through the code path built for M1's frozen buffer (a `zero_damping` flag that bypasses `softplus`, since `softplus(g_raw)` can never be exactly 0 for finite `g_raw`), drive both with N(0,1) inputs (length 512, stream `fixtures:input` seed 0) from N(0,1) initial states (`fixtures:init`), assert outputs are nonzero and bitwise identical to the M1 configuration in fp32 (nonzero-input case registered v1.13 — a zero trajectory would pass vacuously). Guarantees M1 and M1b differ only in dissipation.\\n4. `test_cell_matches_jax_fixtures`. Sequential PyTorch cells reproduce the committed reference trajectories from the official JAX implementations at rtol 1e-5, atol 1e-8 (v1.13). Pinned oracles (v1.6): tk-rusch/linoss @ `05a835355439ee5500b2c8f891132c53adf020c0`, jaredbmit/damped-linoss @ `450b546f693918fe7cfe44082e88538fb29fbd64`; `gen_jax_fixtures.py` runs in a throwaway uv env pinned to `jax==0.4.35` (numpy version recorded), checks out exactly these commits, records versions, shapes, seeds, and dtype in the npz metadata, and generates both undamped and damped cases (G = 0, G = 1e-2; `A` from the registered log-spaced period init, m = 64, drawn via stream `fixtures:a`; `B` and GLU weights N(0, 0.02) via streams `fixtures:b` and `fixtures:glu`) on N(0,1) inputs from stream `fixtures:input`, seeds {0, 1}, length 512, fp64 (v1.7; every parameter stream-determined as of v1.10). Workflow per Appendix G.\\n5. `test_scan_equals_sequential`. Runs (and gates G2) only if a parallel scan implementation exists in the repo; it must match the sequential oracle at rtol 1e-5, atol 1e-8 on N(0,1) inputs of shape (batch 4, length 512, m 64), fp32, stream `fixtures:input` seed 0 (v1.13). The sequential loop is the oracle forever. (Sequential is acceptable for v1 speed. Scan is an optimization, gated by this test when present.)\\n6. `test_gate_identity_recovers_baseline_bitwise`. Build M1 and B0-local from the same seed with shared-submodule init (the base transformer is constructed first from `seed_init` so both variants consume identical RNG streams for shared modules; pathway modules draw from a separate derived generator), force the gate multiplier to exactly 1.0 via a bypass flag (not by driving the sigmoid), and assert forward logits on one Task A batch (batch 8, the (512, 8) cell, `seed_rules = 0, seed_data = 0`, v1.13) are bitwise identical in fp32. Repeat for B1's gate bypassed to 1.0.\\n7. `test_cue_unreachable_exact_zero_grad`. B0-local, fp32, untrained models from seeds {0, 1, 2}, the first 3 eval-stream sequences from each unreachable cell (N = 512 and N = 2048; sample count and fixture identity registered v1.13). For every answer-decision position, compute the Jacobian of the full vocab logit vector with respect to the input-embedding activation at the cue position (the activation at that position, not the embedding table row). Assert every entry is exactly zero, and assert the gradient object is a real zero tensor, not `None` (a `None`/detached graph fails the test — it means the path was never connected, which would make the test vacuous). Repeat for B1. Then assert the same Jacobian is nonzero for M1, M1b, and B2 at the same placements. After Phase 3 training, rerun this test on the trained B0-local and B1 checkpoints as a regression guard. This is the load-bearing proof test.\\n8. `test_cue_reachable_when_close`. Same machinery with the cue placed so the cue-to-decision distance is exactly `receptive_field()` (reachable by one path): gradient nonzero for B0-local. Guards against a masking bug that silently blinds the model everywhere, and pins the boundary convention.\\n9. `test_param_match_within_1pct` across the six variant configs, and generation of `results/params.md` (Section 5.5).\\n\\nNon-vacuity rule (v1.9, instantiated v1.10): every Phase 2 test restates its registered cases and tolerances from this spec in its docstring, counts the cases it actually executed, and asserts that count equals the registered count; tensors nonempty, autograd graphs connected (a `None` gradient is a test failure, never a pass), assertions executed per registered case and seed — no proof test can pass by silently skipping its subject.\\n\\nResidual-determinism rule (v1.10, global): any implementation choice this file leaves open defaults to the deterministic lowest-index / lexicographic / first-in-stream option, recorded in the ledger when exercised — no residual choice may depend on iteration order of unordered containers, wall clock, or hardware.\\n\\nGate G2: tests 1 through 9 plus 2b green (5 when present). Exit: green, commit. These tests are permanent regression guards, never deleted.\\n\\n## Phase 3. Toy proof runs\\n\\n\\n| work | what it established | distance from Stencil |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| Qwen Gated Attention, Qiu et al., NeurIPS 2025, github.com/qiuzh20/gated_attention, deployed in Qwen3-Next | head-specific sigmoid gate after SDPA improves quality, stability, long context, gains attributed to nonlinearity and sparsity, 30 variants at 15B MoE / 1.7B dense on 3.5T tokens | same gate site, stateless gate computed from the current hidden state. This is B1 verbatim. Stencil's delta is the stateful recurrent controller |\\n| Samba, Ren et al., ICLR 2025, arXiv 2406.07522, github.com/microsoft/Samba, and the wider hybrid family (Jamba, Zamba, Nemotron-H) | a recurrent pathway interleaved with sliding-window attention carries information far beyond the window at 3.8B / 3.2T, perfect 256K passkey recall | content configuration, the recurrence writes representations into the residual stream. Stencil's recurrence writes nothing and only modulates |\\n| Mega, Ma et al., arXiv 2209.10655, and Megalodon, arXiv 2404.08801 | damped (Mega) and complex-damped (Megalodon CEMA) moving-average recurrence shaping gated attention, competitive with Llama2 at 7B / 2T | closest single ancestor. Recurrence is content-entangled (feeds Q/K and output gating), damped by construction, never causally analyzed. Also the strongest evidence for the H2 prior favoring damping |\\n| LinOSS, Rusch and Rus, arXiv 2410.03943, and D-LinOSS, arXiv 2505.12171 | forced-harmonic-oscillator SSMs, stable, universal, scan-parallel. D-LinOSS shows rigid dissipation limits representation, forgetting is crucial for long-range reasoning, learnable damping wins | supplies the cell. Neither work uses the oscillator as a control pathway over a transformer |\\n| Zoology / MQAR, Arora et al., 2023, github.com/HazyResearch/zoology, plus B'MOJO, arXiv 2407.06324, and FoX, arXiv 2503.02130 | MQAR as the calibrated recall synthetic correlating with LM quality, the state-size vs recall tradeoff, and the beyond-window drop-to-chance argument stated rhetorically | Task M imports the structure. Task A replaces value retrieval with rule application, meaning control not content. The zero-grad harness operationalizes what B'MOJO argues in prose |\\n| NM-RNN (Costacurta et al., 2024), task-conditioned hypernetworks (von Oswald et al., 2019), HyperRNN (Ha et al., 2016), NeuMoSync (2026) | a slow neuromodulatory controller multiplicatively scaling a target network's weights, low-dimensional context switches framing | concept ancestors, RNN-era or continual-learning-focused, not oscillatory, not gating transformer attention, no necessity proof. NM-RNN reportedly forgets quickly under sequential training, worth citing when discussing Task B |\\n| S2-Net, arXiv 2605.01656, and the oscillatory SNN line | rhythmic timing as a top-down control mechanism, in spiking networks | nearest neuroscience-faithful implementation of waves-as-control, different substrate entirely |\\n| Wave-RNN, arXiv 2309.08045, and Huginn, arXiv 2502.05171 | waves encode the recent past in RNNs, latent recurrence scales test-time compute | context for the writeup's framing, not direct competitors |\\n\\n## Appendix G. Consequently, later queries can recover the rule from a recent gold answer rather than retain the instruction. Multiple queries per span make this a recurring implicit reinsertion channel.
