In a cue-only interval, decisions at lags 253–511 are causally blind—roughly half the cycle. A strong prompt incumbent would reinsert at compaction boundaries, within the receptive field, or immediately before queries. Moreover, a drought cannot make a copy of the “currently active instruction” stale when no update occurs; it merely becomes inaccessible between copies. Register a query-time policy and a refresh/cost sweep, including intervals no larger than 252.\nplan/taskd/review-r1.md:11:4. **critical — The adequacy gate conditions away the failures being measured.** A reinsertion run with queries outside the 252-token receptive field is unlikely to reach 99% on the proposed ID distribution, while persistent-path contenders can. Filtering adequate seeds can also turn oscillator adoption variance into flattering conditional accuracy—the exact danger illustrated by Phase 3’s extreme M1 seed variance. Architecture spec\n\n### 5.1 Base transformer (shared by all variants)\n\n| item | value |\n|---|---|\n| type | decoder-only, pre-LN, causal |\n| d_model | 256 |\n| layers L | 4 |\n| heads H | 4 (head_dim 64) |\n| d_ff | 1024 (adjusted per variant for param matching, see 5.5) |\n| positional | RoPE |\n| attention | causal sliding window, w = 64 (B0-full uses full causal) |\n| dropout | none |\n| vocab | 64 synthetic tokens (see task spec) |\n| params | ~3.2M |\n\nThe exact attention receptive field after L layers is `L * (w - 1) = 252` positions of maximal lag (v1.6); `L * w = 256` is the conservative bound used when placing unreachable cues. These numbers are load-bearing. `model.receptive_field()` returns `L * (w - 1)`; recompute in code and use it in tests, never hardcode 252 or 256 in tests.\n\nBase-model details, all fixed (v1.6): MLP is GELU with no biases anywhere (attention QKVO and MLP); pre-LN LayerNorm plus a final LayerNorm, eps 1e-5; embedding and LM head untied; rope_theta 10000; every weight initialized N(0, 0.02) with the seeded init generator; no dropout anywhere.\n\n### 5.2 Control pathway (M1 and M1b, unified cell)\n\nA stack of oscillatory state-space cells running left-to-right over the token embeddings, independent of the transformer's residual stream. Independence is deliberate. The control state is then a deterministic function of the input sequence alone, which makes causal patching in Phase 4 clean.\n\nContinuous system per cell, diagonal `A >= 0`, diagonal damping `G >= 0`, input `u_t` = token embedding (256):\n\n```\ny'(t) = z(t)\nz'(t) = -A y(t) - G z(t) + B u(t)\n```\n\nDiscretization is symplectic in the conservative part with the damping treated implicitly, so `G = 0` recovers the conservative IMEX update through the identical code path:\n\n```\nz_{k+1} = ( z_k + dt * (-A y_k + B u_k) ) / (1 + dt * G)\ny_{k+1} = y_k + dt * z_{k+1}\n```\n\nNumerical facts, registered so the tests are honest (v1.4). This update is symplectic Euler with implicit damping. With `G = 0` it does NOT conserve the continuous energy `H = z^2 + A y^2` — at `dt = 1` and period 8 the per-step excursion of `H` is tens of percent — it exactly conserves a modified discrete quadratic invariant (for symplectic Euler on `y'' = -A y`, the shifted energy `H_d = z^2 + A y^2 - dt * A * y * z`; derive and verify the exact form for this code path during implementation and record it in a code comment). \"Conservative\" throughout this plan means: the discrete invariant is exactly conserved, hence trajectories are bounded for all time and nothing is forgotten; it does not mean pointwise conservation of the continuous `H`. Stability requires `dt * sqrt(A) < 2`; period_min = 8 gives `dt * sqrt(A) = 2 * pi / 8 ~ 0.785`, satisfied with margin, and `A` is re-checked against the bound after training. Closed-form comparisons in tests use the exact discrete solution (matrix power of the one-step map in fp64), not the continuous solution.\n\nVerify both the undamped and damped forms against the LinOSS (arXiv 2410.03943) and D-LinOSS (arXiv 2505.12171) equations during implementation. If they differ materially, record the discrepancy and the chosen resolution as a review-gated amendment (Autonomy policy) — external code never silently overrides the governing equations. Cross-check numerically against committed JAX fixtures per Appendix G (pinned commits and versions listed there).\n\nTensor shapes, fixed (v1.4). Cell 1: `B_1 in R^{64 x 256}` reads token embeddings; states `y_1, z_1 in R^64`, initialized to zeros. Between cells: GLU `u_2 = (W_a y_1) * sigmoid(W_b y_1)` with `W_a, W_b in R^{64 x 64}`. Cell 2: `B_2 in R^{64 x 64}` reads `u_2`; states `y_2, z_2 in R^64`, zeros init. The control output is `c_t = [y_2 ; z_2] in R^128` — the final cell's full state, no extra readout (the \"readout\" is the gate projection in 5.3). Phase 4's probed and patched object `c` is exactly this `c_t`. Per-cell parameters `a_raw, g_raw in R^64`. No biases on `B_i`, `W_a`, `W_b`.\n\n| item | value |\n|---|---|\n| oscillator pairs m | 64 (state dim 128: y and z each 64) |\n| cells stacked | 2, with a GLU nonlinearity between, per LinOSS block structure |\n| dt | 1.0 (frequencies absorb scale) |\n| frequency init | `sqrt(A)` log-spaced so periods span [period_min, period_max] = [8, 2 * longest task delay at this scale] (toy: [8, 4096]; Phase 6: [8, 16384]) |\n| A parameterization | `A = softplus(a_raw)` elementwise, keeps A >= 0 |\n| G parameterization | `G = softplus(g_raw)` elementwise, keeps G >= 0 |\n| G in M1 | frozen buffer of exact zeros (not a parameter) |\n| G in M1b | learnable, `g_raw` init -9 (G ~ 1.2e-4) |\n| B_i, W_a, W_b init | N(0, 0.02), no biases (shapes in the v1.4 tensor table below) |\n| stability | `dt * sqrt(A) < 2` required at init and at every gated checkpoint (validity condition, Appendix C) |\n\nThe log-spaced period range must bracket every delay used in the tasks at the scale being trained, which is why period_max is parameterized rather than fixed. This is the \"slow control field\" claim made concrete. Frequencies are learned but initialized slow. The M1b damping init is deliberately near-conservative (retention over 2048 steps roughly 0.7 at init) so early training matches M1 and gradient descent discovers useful dissipation, which is the fair test of H2, rather than initializing M1b already forgetting.\n\n### 5.3 Gate application (recurrent variants)\n\nControl output `c_t = [y_2 ; z_2]` (dim 128, the final cell's full state per the Section 5.2 tensor table) maps to per-layer, per-head gates:\n\n```\ng[l, h, t] = 2 * sigmoid(W_g[l,h] · c_t + b_g[l,h])      # scalar per (layer, head, position)\nhead_out[l, h, t] *= g[l, h, t]                           # after attention, before W_O concat\n```\n\n16 gates total (4 layers x 4 heads). `c_t` is the final cell's `[y_2 ; z_2]` per the Section 5.2 tensor table (v1.6, removing the stale \"final cell's y\" wording). Gates initialize near 1: `b_g = 0` gives g = 1.0 at c = 0, and `W_g` init N(0, 1e-3) (registered v1.6) so early training matches baseline behavior. MLP gating is out of scope for v1.\n\n### 5.4 Variants\n\n| id | attention | gate pathway | purpose |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| B0-full | full causal | none | ceiling reference, efficiency comparison |\n| B0-local | window 64 | none | provably-at-chance control |\n| B1 | window 64 | Qwen G1 headwise: per layer, `g[l,h,t] = sigmoid(w[l,h] · x_norm[l,t])` where `x_norm[l,t]` is that layer's post-norm attention input, gate multiplies the head output after SDPA | provably-at-chance beyond the window, isolates statefulness against the published, deployed stateless mechanism (Qiu et al., NeurIPS 2025, see Appendix F). All share the base transformer code path. M1 and M1b must be the same cell class differing only in whether `G` is a frozen zero buffer or a parameter. B2 is a deliberately different architecture (first-order, no oscillation, no GLU stack) and is compared as such per H2's v1.4 wording. Init fairness note, B2's λ init moved from 0.99 to 0.999 in v1.1 so the variants with learnable dissipation (M1b, B2) start in a slow-forgetting regime and learn their forgetting rate; M1's dissipation is frozen at zero by design as the conservative pole.\n\n### 5.5 Parameter matching\n\nCounting rule: `count_params()` counts all trainable parameters (frozen buffers such as M1's `G` excluded, embeddings included). The 90-bar remains binding only for phase gates on the science.\\n\\nCross-model review, kimi (v1.6). kimi-k3 (`kimi-k3:cloud` via the local ollama daemon) is the second, independent reviewer: `python3 tools/run_kimi_review.py <phase> <topic> <threshold>` writes `plan/reviews/<phase>/<topic>-kimi.md` under the same round-log, append-only, and severity contracts, serialized on the same lock. Cadence: at least one kimi cross-review per phase on the gate-critical work, plus each retrospective (threshold 75 there). kimi is advisory — sol remains reviewer of record and kimi acceptance is not required for gates — but the orchestrator verifies kimi's high/critical claims and injects confirmed ones into sol's next round for adjudication; a confirmed, unrefuted kimi finding must be resolved like any other. Tie-break: when the orchestrator and sol deadlock on a finding after two full resolve-or-refute round trips, kimi receives the finding text VERBATIM, the fix or refutation evidence, and both arguments verbatim (summaries are forbidden — the vacated batch 4 shows why), and renders a verdict; the verdict is executed and ledger-recorded. Trigger order, reconciled (v1.22): two deadlocked round trips → kimi tie-break; sol disputing an EXECUTED tie-break in its next round → human touchpoint; a second dispute after a human ruling is out of scope for review. Mandatory human touchpoint (1) of the Autonomy policy now triggers only if sol's next round disputes the executed tie-break.\\n\\nReview-session continuity (v1.6). One review (one phase/topic file) is served by ONE reviewer session across all of its rounds: round 1 records the codex thread id (plan/reviews/.sessions/, machine-local, gitignored) and every later round resumes it, so the reviewer keeps its original context and re-verifies its own findings against the diffs instead of re-litigating from scratch. Anti-churn rule, binding on reviewers: rounds after the first re-examine existing findings and the changes; new findings are added only for regressions introduced by fixes or clear in-scope misses from the original review — scope never expands round-over-round. A new review (next phase or topic) starts a fresh session and then holds it for its own rounds. If a stored session is unusable, the wrapper falls back to a fresh run carrying the prior review file, noted in the wrapper log; the orchestrator MUST append the continuity-loss note to plan/LEDGER.md in the same working session (v1.18 — the log alone is not the audit record). kimi is stateless; its continuity is the prior rounds inlined in each call plus the same anti-churn rule.\\n\\nPhase retrospectives and agent evals (v1.6). After each phase's exit commit, before the next phase starts, the orchestrator writes `plan/retros/<phase>.md`: what went well and what went poorly, with evidence (finding counts and severities per round, fix attempts, reruns, wrapper failures, wall clock vs budget), root causes, and concrete optimizations. Every optimization lands as a diff in the retro commit — the AGENTS.md diff is quoted inside the retro document so the kimi retro review audits it (v1.19), an AGENTS.md entry (the agent playbook codex auto-loads and CLAUDE.md imports), a tooling or prompt fix under tools/, or a deferral ledgered with reason; changes to governed content still go through the amendment path. kimi reviews each retro (advisory, threshold 75) against one rubric question: does the retro assign blame where the evidence points. Performance is measured, not self-reported: `tools/agent_metrics.py` computes, from reviewer-authored review files and git history, first-round scores, rounds-to-acceptance, findings-per-round by severity, and open high/critical counts; the retro records the trend plus two hand-counted metrics, escaped defects (a finding whose root cause was accepted in an earlier phase) and lesson recurrence (a new finding matching an existing AGENTS.md lesson — the direct measure of whether the improvement loop works; target zero). Metrics are advisory and never gate science.\\n\\nAutonomy policy (v1.5). The project runs autonomously by default; honesty is enforced by the adversarial review protocol above and by the deterministic proof tests, not by human checkpoints. Concretely: wherever this plan says an amendment or decision is \\\"human-authorized,\\\" the autonomous path is that the orchestrator drafts the amendment with rationale, a sol@xhigh review of it is run (topic `amendment`, same wrapper), and it takes effect only once that review is accepted with zero open high/critical findings; the ledger records it and the human can audit asynchronously. Threshold freezes at first run launch remain absolute against evidence-driven rescue — no review can undo a freeze; the sole exception is the Adjudication-5 repair clause below (mathematically unpassable constants, init-time proof, no governed data). Binary-artifact descriptions (v1.27, formalizing the batch-5 presentation contract): every PRESENT binary gate artifact carries a prose sidecar at `results/<slug>-description.md` (key inventory, shapes, dtypes, provenance, current sha256, consumer) — reaching kimi through the standing results/*.md context glob; review directories hold only review files (the acceptance layout rule). Agents: Claude Opus (max effort, web research + on-machine empirical probes), codex gpt-5.6-sol @ xhigh (code close-read), kimi-k3 (independent analysis, source inlined). Orchestrator cross-ranking and the applied decision live in the ledger and tools/codex-agents/phase3-perf.md.\\n\\n---\\n## Report A: sol @ xhigh\\n# Performance report\\n\\n## Executive conclusion\\n\\nM1’s remaining slowdown is dominated by the oscillator controller, specifically launch-heavy eager execution inside the “parallel” scan.\\n\\nAt batch 8, the recorded banded timings are:\\n\\n- B0-local: 0.112 s/step\\n- M1: 0.316 s/step\\n\\nThat attributes roughly 65% of M1 wall time to the controller and gating path. At batch 64, 0.40 steps/s versus the roughly 1.1-step/s baseline gives the same conclusion and establishes a hard upper bound of about 2.75× if controller overhead vanished entirely.\\n\\nThe current scan still executes:\\n\\n- 256 Python iterations to summarize blocks;\\n- 256 Python iterations to replay blocks;\\n- two oscillator cells;\\n- therefore 1,024 Python iterations per M1 forward, each containing several eager fp32 operations, followed by a correspondingly fragmented backward graph.\\n\\nMy first three actions would be:\\n\\n1. Compile the oscillator controller, then the full model, with static shapes and `fullgraph=True`.\\n2. If compilation does not reduce controller time by at least roughly 3×, replace the two scan loops with a deterministic fused device-side scan and fixed-order backward.\\n3. Remove step-level graph breaks/synchronizations and CUDA-graph the complete forward/backward/clip/AdamW step.\\n\\nA realistic combined target is approximately 0.7–1.0 steps/s, not the product of the individual speedups below.\\n\\nExpected speedups are estimates relative to the current path and are not additive.\\n\\n## Ranked recommendations\\n\\n| Rank | Optimization | Expected effect |\\n|---:|---|---:|\\n| 1 | Compile controller/full model | 1.25–1.7× whole-M1 |\\n| 2 | Deterministic fused blocked scan if compilation is insufficient | 1.6–2.3× whole-M1 from current; smaller incremental gain after compilation |\\n| 3 | Capture-safe step plus CUDA Graph | 1.10–1.35× incremental |\\n| 4 | True block-sparse/window attention kernel | 1.05–1.20× M1; 1.3–2.0× local baselines |\\n| 5 | Normalize/project all gates once; pack controller GLU | 1.03–1.10× M1 |\\n| 6 | Fused or foreach AdamW | 1.02–1.08× |\\n| 7 | Cache RoPE/masks and pack QKV; remove unused outputs | 1.03–1.10× combined |\\n| 8 | Vectorized/prefetched data and asynchronous metric logging | 1.03–1.06× |\\n| 9 | B2/B4-specific obvious overheads | Potentially 1.2–1.6× for those variants |\\n| 10 | Two-run matrix co-tenancy | 0–20% aggregate, highly profile-dependent |\\n\\n## 1. Compile the controller, then the model\\n\\nThe best low-intrusion experiment is `torch.compile` around [OscillatorController.forward](/home/bmarti44/stencil-llm/src/stencil/oscillator.py:470), initially without compiling the optimizer or data path.\\n\\nWhy it should help:\\n\\n- Both 256-step loops in [OscillatorCell._forward_scan](/home/bmarti44/stencil-llm/src/stencil/oscillator.py:217) have static trip counts.\\n- The nine-block recursive scan has static depth.\\n- The four transformer layers and five attention chunks are static loops.\\n- Most of the scan body is pointwise arithmetic suitable for vertical fusion.\\n- The controller’s GLU, RMS normalization, gates, residuals, GELU, and RoPE contain many additional fusion opportunities.\\n\\nFor M1, the model forward has no inherent data-dependent graph break. The B4-only `.item()` branch is not taken because M1 passes `cue_mask=None` into banded attention. Static Python loops should be specialized/unrolled; the risk is an extremely large FX/AOTAutograd graph, not a semantic graph break.\\n\\nRecommended sequence:\\n\\n1. Compile only `model.controller` with `fullgraph=True, dynamic=False`.\\n2. Inspect graph breaks and generated-kernel count.\\n3. Try the complete `StencilTransformer`.\\n4. Prefer normal compilation for fusion; use manual CUDA Graph capture later rather than immediately selecting a reduce-overhead mode.\\n\\nPyTorch recommends `fullgraph=True` specifically to expose graph breaks. Static loops can be specialized, while data-dependent tensor control cannot. [PyTorch compile guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/user_guide/torch_compiler/compile/programming_model.fullgraph_true.html)\\n\\nDeterminism/fp32 risk: medium. Inductor may introduce FMA or remove intermediate roundings. PyTorch 2.13 automatically enables its deterministic compiler mode when deterministic algorithms are active, disabling numerically sensitive autotuning, but this does not promise equality with eager output. [Deterministic algorithms documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.use_deterministic_algorithms.html)\\n\\nEquality gate:\\n\\n- Keep the eager model callable as the oracle.\\n- Compare compiled/eager forward output and input/parameter gradients at lengths 512 and 2051, fp32, with `rtol=1e-5` and the existing per-operation `atol`.\\n- Assert every candidate output, gradient, and optimizer state remains fp32.\\n- Run two candidate 50-step M1 trainings and require bitwise-equal losses and final `state_dict`s.\\n- Retain the existing bitwise M1/M1b zero-damping and gate-identity tests.\\n\\n## 2. Fuse the blocked oscillator scan device-side\\n\\nIf compilation does not collapse the scan adequately, the main implementation change belongs in [OscillatorCell._forward_scan](/home/bmarti44/stencil-llm/src/stencil/oscillator.py:217).\\n\\nThe current scan is block-parallel, but it is not launch-efficient:\\n\\n- Lines 257–267 perform many eager operations 256 times.\\n- Lines 279–286 repeat another recurrence 256 times.\\n- M1 does this twice.\\n- Each stored `y` and `z` is later copied into a stack.\\n- At length 2051, padding to 2304 causes about 12% useless tail work.\\n- The homogeneous transition is redundantly represented across all nine blocks even though it is identical for every block.\\n- The nine blocks require eight logical affine compositions. [_scan_affine_2x2](/home/bmarti44/stencil-llm/src/stencil/oscillator.py:50) implements these with a depth-four recursive tree, but each mathematical composition expands into many tiny eager kernels, slices, stacks, and concatenations.\\n\\nA good fused design would use:\\n\\n1. One device program per `(batch, block, mode)` that loops through the 256 positions locally and emits the block affine summary.\\n2. One small kernel per `(batch, mode)` that serially composes the eight inter-block transitions in a fixed order. With only nine blocks, a serial device loop is cheaper than an eager recursive tree.\\n3. One output kernel that replays each block locally and writes the trajectories.\\n4. A special partial-tail path so the ninth block executes only its three or four real positions.\\n5. A custom backward with fixed-order reductions. Parameter-gradient atomics must not be used.\\n\\nThe installed internal associative-scan implementation is not sufficient: its own 2.13 source marks it prototype and unsupported by autograd. It is therefore not a drop-in training solution.\\n\\nExpected speedup: 1.6–2.3× for the complete current M1 step. The theoretical ceiling is about 2.75–2.83× because the base transformer remains.\\n\\nDeterminism/fp32 risk: high. A Triton/CUDA backward could easily introduce nondeterministic atomic accumulation or fast-math differences. Use IEEE fp32 operations, fixed reduction trees, and no atomics. Emit per-batch/block partial gradients and reduce them deterministically.\\n\\nEquality gate:\\n\\n- Preserve `_forward_sequential` permanently.\\n- Extend `test_scan_equals_sequential` beyond its current forward-only check to compare gradients for inputs, `B`, `a_raw`, and `g_raw`.\\n- Test zero and nonzero initial states, both damping modes, lengths 512 and 2051.\\n- Use `rtol=1e-5`, `atol=1e-8` for trajectories and a justified small absolute tolerance for gradients.\\n- Run the candidate twice bitwise, including final parameters after a short real training.\\n- Re-run the JAX fixture, damping-zero bitwise, stability, and energy tests.\\n\\n## 3. Make the step CUDA-graph eligible\\n\\nThe M1 compute graph is fundamentally captureable, but [train_model](/home/bmarti44/stencil-llm/src/stencil/train.py:162) is not captureable as written.\\n\\nCurrent blockers and barriers:\\n\\n- [masked_answer_loss](/home/bmarti44/stencil-llm/src/stencil/train.py:109) converts `torch.any(decisions)` into Python control, forcing a device synchronization.\\n- Boolean indexing with `logits[..., decisions]` produces a data-dependent output shape.\\n- `float(loss.detach())` at line 195 synchronizes every step.\\n- The callback performs JSON serialization and `flush()` every step.\\n- New GPU input tensors are allocated by `.to()` each step rather than copied into static buffers.\\n- AdamW uses `capturable=False`.\\n- The LR is a changing Python float stored in optimizer dictionaries.\\n- Task B can produce changing padded lengths, although the registered Task A/M matrix cells have fixed lengths.\\n\\nRequired changes:\\n\\n- Have `Batch` carry fixed-shape decision positions and targets. Gather `[batch, decisions, vocab]` logits directly instead of using a boolean mask.\\n- Use static GPU token/decision buffers and `copy_` each new batch into them.\\n- Store the LR in a CUDA scalar tensor accepted by a capturable optimizer.\\n- Capture forward, selected loss, backward, clipping, and optimizer update.\\n- Copy losses asynchronously to a pinned CPU ring and write them in chunks. Do not call `.item()` every step.\\n- Keep data generation and static-buffer fills outside capture.\\n\\nCUDA Graphs are appropriate here because they replay the whole kernel sequence with one CPU launch. They require fixed shapes/addresses, prohibit `.item()`, and prohibit dynamic CPU/GPU control. [PyTorch CUDA Graph constraints](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/cuda.html)\\n\\nExpected speedup: 1.2–1.6× on the current eager scan, or roughly 1.10–1.35× after compiler fusion.\\n\\nDeterminism/fp32 risk: low to medium. A graph normally replays the same kernels in the same order. The optimizer and any new loss-gather formulation are the main numerical changes.\\n\\nEquality gate:\\n\\n- Compare one eager and graphed step from identical model/optimizer states: loss, all gradients, optimizer states, and updated parameters.\\n- Require candidate-vs-oracle `rtol=1e-5`.\\n- Require two complete graphed 50-step runs to be bitwise identical.\\n- Verify chunked `metrics.jsonl` contains exactly the same ordered `(step, loss, lr)` records.\\n- Test capture at both registered Task A and Task M shapes.\\n\\n## 4. Replace the pseudo-banded attention with true sparse attention\\n\\nThe current query block is 512 tokens: [Attention.__init__](/home/bmarti44/stencil-llm/src/stencil/model.py:17) sets `8 * window`.\\n\\nFor length 2051 and window 64, the five SDPA calls compute about 1,145,542 query-key pairs per head. Only about 129,248 pairs are actually allowed. Thus the current path still computes roughly 8.9× the ideal local-window work.\\n\\nThe existing GB10 sweep already tested blocks of 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16 windows and found eight windows fastest. Simply changing 512 to 64 would reduce arithmetic but lose badly to extra launches. I would retain 512 for this implementation.\\n\\nThe next useful step is a different kernel:\\n\\n- First test PyTorch 2.13 `flex_attention` with a cached block mask for `q >= k` and `q-k < 64`.\\n- Use a 64-token sparse block.\\n- Enable the deterministic block-sparse backward metadata available in the installed 2.13 implementation.\\n- If fp32 FlexAttention is not competitive or cannot satisfy determinism, use a custom deterministic local-attention kernel.\\n- For B4, precompute padded cue positions separately; its batch-dependent global columns complicate a reusable block mask.\\n\\nExpected speedup: 1.3–2.0× for B0-local/B1, but only 1.05–1.20× for M1 because attention is now about one-third of M1 wall time.\\n\\nDeterminism/fp32 risk: medium/high. Sparse attention changes softmax accumulation order. SDPA backends also have distinct determinism characteristics; with strict deterministic mode PyTorch selects or forces deterministic paths, but equality across backends is not bitwise. [PyTorch reproducibility and SDPA](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/notes/randomness.html)\\n\\nEquality gate:\\n\\n- Keep the current banded SDPA path and full-mask path as oracles.\\n- Retain the existing eight forward cases at `rtol=1e-5`, `atol=1e-7`.\\n- Add backward comparisons for Q, K, V, projection weights, and input.\\n- Require two short training runs to remain bitwise deterministic.\\n- Retain the B4 exact key-set reconstruction.\\n\\n## 5. Fuse controller GLU and gate projection\\n\\nTwo concrete redundancies exist.\\n\\nFirst, [project_control_gate](/home/bmarti44/stencil-llm/src/stencil/gates.py:18) recomputes the RMS normalization of the full `[B,T,128]` control tensor once per transformer layer. That is four identical square/reduce/sqrt/divide paths and four corresponding backward graphs.\\n\\nNormalize once before the block loop, flatten `gate_weight` from `[L,H,128]` to `[L*H,128]`, and compute all 16 gates with one linear projection and one sigmoid. Reshape to `[B,T,L,H]`.\\n\\nSecond, [OscillatorController.forward](/home/bmarti44/stencil-llm/src/stencil/oscillator.py:470) performs two separate 64→64 linears for the GLU. Pack `W_a` and `W_b` into one 64→128 projection, split it, and fuse sigmoid/multiply through compilation.\\n\\nLayerNorm itself is already a fused PyTorch operation. I would not replace it with a custom norm or RMSNorm—the latter changes the model. Let the compiler fuse residual/normalization epilogues where legal.\\n\\nExpected speedup: 1.03–1.10× M1.\\n\\nDeterminism/fp32 risk: medium. Reusing one normalization changes gradient accumulation order; packed GEMMs may use a different tiling.\\n\\nEquality gate:\\n\\n- Compare all gates, logits, control/input gradients, and gate weights against the current functions.\\n- Require `rtol=1e-5`.\\n- Keep `test_gate_identity_recovers_baseline_bitwise` bitwise.\\n- Verify the packed initialization consumes exactly the same RNG values or convert existing separate parameters without changing initialization order.\\n\\n## 6. Enable foreach or fused AdamW\\n\\n[_optimizer](/home/bmarti44/stencil-llm/src/stencil/train.py:127) explicitly forces the slowest AdamW implementation:\\n\\n```python\\nforeach=False,\\nfused=False,\\n```\\n\\nM1 has roughly 52 parameter tensors, many tiny. The single-tensor AdamW path issues multiple kernels for each tensor. Try, in order:\\n\\n1. `foreach=True, fused=False`\\n2. `foreach=False, fused=True`\\n3. `fused=True, capturable=True` for CUDA Graph capture\\n\\nPyTorch 2.13 documents fp32 support for fused AdamW and describes fused as providing vertical and horizontal fusion. [AdamW documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.optim.AdamW)\\n\\nGradient clipping already defaults to the faster foreach implementation on CUDA, so it is not the first optimizer-side target.\\n\\nExpected speedup: 1.02–1.08× whole step, potentially more after the controller is accelerated.\\n\\nDeterminism/fp32 risk: medium. Both are eligible in fp32, but the deterministic flag is not a promise that fused output equals the old optimizer numerically. It should fail loudly for known unsupported nondeterminism, but empirical bitwise testing remains mandatory.\\n\\nEquality gate:\\n\\n- Feed identical synthetic gradients to reference and candidate AdamW states for 100 updates.\\n- Compare parameters and moment buffers after every update at `rtol=1e-5`.\\n- Test both weight-decay groups.\\n- Require two real candidate trainings to match each other bitwise.\\n\\n## 7. Remove smaller recomputation and memory traffic\\n\\nSpecific opportunities:\\n\\n- [_rope](/home/bmarti44/stencil-llm/src/stencil/model.py:37) recomputes frequencies, positions, angles, sine, and cosine independently for Q and K in every layer. Build one device/dtype-specific RoPE cache and share it across all layers.\\n- Banded masks and `arange` tensors are reconstructed in every layer. Cache the five local masks for a fixed run length.\\n- Q, K, and V are three separate projections reading the same normalized activation. A packed QKV parameter reduces GEMM launches and input traffic.\\n- [StencilTransformer.forward](/home/bmarti44/stencil-llm/src/stencil/model.py:325) computes a cue mask for every variant, although M1, M1b, B0, B1, and B2 do not use it in attention. Construct it only for B3/B4.\\n- The first oscillator cell returns and stacks its entire `z1` trajectory even though `OscillatorController` discards it.\\n- The model produces final-norm and LM-head logits for all 2051 positions, then trains on one Task A position or eight Task M positions. Select hidden states before final norm/head.\\n- The final answer token is not required as a causal input; the current trainer forwards the full token sequence and slices logits afterward.\\n\\nExpected combined speedup: 1.03–1.10×.\\n\\nRisk: low for mask/cue/output removal; medium for packed QKV and RoPE cache. Compute the cache on the target GPU in fp32—CPU-generated trigonometric values may not equal the retained CUDA path closely enough.\\n\\nEquality gate: selected logits and all relevant gradients against the current full-logit path, plus the existing attention, Jacobian, and gate-identity tests.\\n\\n## 8. Data pipeline and metric overlap\\n\\nThe current pipeline is entirely synchronous:\\n\\n- `next_examples` creates 64 Python examples, metadata dictionaries, and padded CPU tensors.\\n- Task A performs roughly 131,000 scalar `torch.randint` calls per batch.\\n- CPU tensors are pageable.\\n- `.to(device)` is not nonblocking.\\n- The GPU is synchronized before the next batch is generated.\\n- Metrics are flushed every step.\\n\\nBecause measured data generation is 6%, its standalone Amdahl ceiling is only 1.064×. It is still worth hiding after GPU launch overhead is reduced.\\n\\nRecommended change:\\n\\n- Use a single deterministic producer and a two- or three-slot pinned-memory ring.\\n- Preserve the original generator schedule exactly.\\n- Copy the next batch with `non_blocking=True`.\\n- Drop training metadata that is never consumed.\\n- Vectorize draws only if a stream-continuation equality test proves that vector and scalar calls consume exactly the same RNG sequence.\\n- Batch metric writes and use asynchronous scalar D2H copies.\\n\\nEquality gate:\\n\\n- Old and new producers must emit byte-identical tokens, masks, and subsequent generator states for multiple batches.\\n- Run both through the exact training consumer, not merely the generator.\\n- Verify identical metrics ordering and no missing final chunk.\\n\\n## 9. Variant-specific issues\\n\\n### B2\\n\\n[DecayCell._forward_scan](/home/bmarti44/stencil-llm/src/stencil/oscillator.py:349) calls the `decay` property inside both 256-step loops. The property executes `sigmoid(raw)` every time—twice per iteration in the first loop and once per iteration in the second, approximately 768 sigmoids per forward.\\n\\nHoist:\\n\\n```python\\ndecay = self.decay\\n```\\n\\nonce before both loops. Do the same in `_forward_sequential`.\\n\\nThis could improve B2 by 1.2–1.6× depending on its controller share. Output should remain bitwise equal; gradients may differ slightly because a single sigmoid node receives accumulated gradients.\\n\\n### B4\\n\\n[_forward_banded](/home/bmarti44/stencil-llm/src/stencil/model.py:99) computes:\\n\\n```python\\nint(cue_mask.sum(dim=1).max().item())\\n```\\n\\nonce per layer, then sorts all sequence positions once per layer. That is four mandatory GPU→CPU synchronizations and four redundant sorts.\\n\\nBuild fixed-width padded cue-position/validity tensors once per batch, preferably on the CPU where tokens originate, and reuse them in all layers. This also removes B4’s `torch.compile` and CUDA Graph blocker.\\n\\nExpected B4 gain: roughly 1.05–1.20×.\\n\\n## 10. Matrix scheduling\\n\\n[execute_pending](/home/bmarti44/stencil-llm/scripts/run_matrix.py:122) runs all 114 cells serially, each in a blocking subprocess.\\n\\nTwo concurrent runs could fill GPU launch gaps, but the earlier 94% utilization report suggests limited headroom. It may instead create context-switching and memory-pressure losses.\\n\\nI would test two-way concurrency only after the single-run path is optimized:\\n\\n- Measure aggregate steps/s for two representative cells.\\n- Require each concurrent run to reproduce a solo run bitwise.\\n- Cap concurrency explicitly; never derive it from CPU count.\\n- Preserve separate run directories and the current restart semantics.\\n\\nExpected aggregate gain: 0–20%; possible regression if kernels already saturate the GPU.\\n\\n## Final assessment\\n\\nThe scan optimization improved asymptotic parallelism but left the dominant implementation problem intact: its sequential work moved from 2051 host iterations to two sets of 256 host iterations per cell, still producing thousands of tiny eager fp32 kernels and a very fragmented backward graph.\\n\\nThe best near-term path is:\\n\\n1. Compile the controller and inspect the generated kernel count.\\n2. Fuse the scan only if compilation fails to collapse those loops.\\n3. Remove the dynamic loss/sync/logging surfaces and graph the entire step.\\n4. Then pursue true block-sparse attention and gate/optimizer fusion.\\n\\nNo files were changed during this audit.\\n---\\n## Report B: kimi-k3\\n# Diagnosis (before the list)\\n\\nBoth variants are **launch/dispatch-bound, not math-bound**. The trunk is ~2.5 TFLOP/step fp32 (GEMMs ~0.83 fwd, banded SDPA math-path ~0.4, ×3 for bwd) — under ~150 ms of ideal GPU work on GB10. The measured 0.91 s/step baseline leaves ~0.75 s of overhead; the oscillator adds ~1.6 s on top. That delta matches its launch count: `_forward_scan` runs **two 256-iteration Python loops × ~8–12 tiny kernels × 2 cells** plus the recursive `_scan_affine_2x2` interleave (stack/flatten/cat storms) — ≈8k launches forward, and autograd re-dispatches ~2× that backward: **~25–30k launches/step on aarch64 with deterministic-mode guards**. That's the 1.6 s. Conclusions: kill launches structurally (scan rewrite) *and* kill the rest of dispatch (CUDA graphs). Everything below preserves fp32; nothing touches math semantics beyond what you already gate at rtol 1e-5.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Ranked optimizations\\n\\n### 1 ★ — Whole-step CUDA-graph capture of the training step\\n**Change:** `train.py::train_model` (new graph runner), plus its enablers: `next_examples` (pad collate to fixed `context_len=2052`, pinned staging + `non_blocking` H2D), `masked_answer_loss` (boolean indexing → `F.cross_entropy(reduction='none') * mask / mask.sum()`; boolean indexing is a host sync and a dynamic shape — both uncapturable), `_optimizer` (`AdamW(..., capturable=True)`, lr as a CUDA fp32 tensor updated via `fill_`), grads preallocated with `set_to_none=False` and zeroed **inside** the capture via `torch._foreach_zero_`, loss readback via a fixed pinned D2H memcpy node (capturable) — so exactly one sync per step remains.\\n**Expected:** m1/m1b: 2.5 s → ~0.3–0.45 s (**~6–8×**); baselines: 0.91 → ~0.55–0.65 s (**~1.4–1.7×**). Replay turns ~30k CPU dispatches into GPU-side scheduling at ~1–2 µs/kernel. Bonus: prefetch the next `next_examples` batch on a CPU thread during async replay → the 6% datagen cost disappears. \\\"weight_decay\\\": config.weight_decay},\\n            {\\\"params\\\": no_decay, \\\"weight_decay\\\": 0.0},\\n        ],\\n        lr=config.lr,\\n        betas=(config.adam_beta1, config.adam_beta2),\\n        eps=config.adam_eps,\\n        foreach=False,\\n        fused=False,\\n    )\\n\\n\\ndef _training_device(device: str | torch.device | None) -> torch.device:\\n    if device is not None:\\n        return torch.device(device)\\n    return torch.device(\\\"cuda\\\" if torch.cuda.is_available() else \\\"cpu\\\")\\n\\n\\ndef train_model(\\n    config: Config,\\n    *,\\n    device: str | torch.device | None = None,\\n    on_step: Callable[[int, float, float], None] | None = None,\\n) -> tuple[StencilTransformer, list[float]]:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Train one real variant using fresh generator data at every step.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    if config.task not in {\\\"a\\\", \\\"b\\\", \\\"m\\\"}:\\n        raise ValueError(\\\"full-variant training requires task a, b, or m\\\")\\n    if config.precision != \\\"fp32\\\":\\n        raise ValueError(\\\"toy-phase training requires fp32\\\")\\n    if config.steps < 1 or config.batch < 1:\\n        raise ValueError(\\\"steps and batch must be positive\\\")\\n    execution_device = _training_device(device)\\n    model = StencilTransformer(config).to(device=execution_device, dtype=torch.float32)\\n    stream = generate(config)\\n    # AdamW itself has no draws; instantiation still pins the registered stream.\\n    named_generator(config.seed_train, \\\"train\\\")\\n    optimizer = _optimizer(model, config)\\n    losses: list[float] = []\\n    model.train()\\n    for step in range(config.steps):\\n        lr = _learning_rate(config, step)\\n        for group in optimizer.param_groups:\\n            group[\\\"lr\\\"] = lr\\n        batch = next_examples(stream, config.batch)\\n        tokens = batch.tokens.to(execution_device)\\n        loss_mask = batch.loss_mask.to(execution_device)\\n        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)\\n        loss = masked_answer_loss(model(tokens), tokens, loss_mask)\\n        loss.backward()\\n        nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), config.clip)\\n        optimizer.step()\\n        value = float(loss.detach())\\n        losses.append(value)\\n        if on_step is not None:\\n            on_step(step, value, lr)\\n    return model, losses\\n\\n\\ndef train_model_losses(\\n    config: Config, *, device: str | torch.device | None = None\\n) -> list[float]:\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"Convenience surface for the full-model determinism contract.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n    model, losses = train_model(config, device=device)\\n    del model\\n    return losses\\n\\n\\ndef _train(config: Config) -> tuple[list[float], list[float]]:\\n    if config.task != \\\"copy\\\":\\n        raise ValueError(\\\"the Phase 0 trainer supports only task='copy'\\\")\\n    if config.precision != \\\"fp32\\\":\\n        raise ValueError(\\\"the Phase 0 trainer requires fp32\\\")\\n\\n    model = initialize_model(config).to(dtype=torch.float32)\\n    operands = named_generator(config.seed_data, \\\"operands\\\")\\n    # Instantiate the registered optimizer stream even though AdamW has no random draws.\\n    named_generator(config.seed_train, \\\"train\\\")\\n    decay = [model.embedding_weight, model.head_weight]\\n    no_decay = [model.head_bias]\\n    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(\\n        [\\n            {\\\"params\\\": decay, \\\"weight_decay\\\": config.weight_decay},\\n            {\\\"params\\\": no_decay, \\\"weight_decay\\\": 0.0},\\n        ],\\n        lr=config.lr,\\n        betas=(config.adam_beta1, config.adam_beta2),\\n        eps=config.adam_eps,\\n    )\\n\\n    losses: list[float] = []\\n    learning_rates: list[float] = []\\n    for step in range(config.steps):\\n        lr = _learning_rate(config, step)\\n        for group in optimizer.param_groups:\\n            group[\\\"lr\\\"] = lr\\n        tokens = _next_batch(config, operands)\\n        logits = model(tokens)\\n        loss = F.cross_entropy(\\n            logits[:, 1:, :].reshape(-1, config.vocab),\\n            tokens[:, :-1].reshape(-1),\\n        )\\n        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)\\n        loss.backward()\\n        nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), config.clip)\\n        optimizer.step()\\n        losses.append(loss.detach().item())\\n        learning_rates.append(lr)\\n    return losses, learning_rates\\n\\n\\ndef _learning_rate(config: Config, step: int) -> float:\\n    if step < config.warmup:\\n        return config.lr * (step + 1) / config.warmup\\n    decay_intervals = max(1, config.steps - config.warmup - 1)\\n    progress = min(1.0, (step - config.warmup) / decay_intervals)\\n    cosine = 0.5 * (1.0 + math.cos(math.pi * progress))\\n    return config.lr_min + (config.lr - config.lr_min) * cosine\\n\\n\\ndef run(\\n    config: Config,\\n    *,\\n    repo: str | Path = \\\".\\\",\\n    force: bool = False,\\n    allow_dirty: bool = False,\\n) -> Path:\\n    root = Path(repo).resolve()\\n    identity = git_identity(root)\\n    if identity.dirty and not allow_dirty:\\n        raise RuntimeError(\\\"dirty worktree requires --allow-dirty\\\")\\n    identifier = make_run_id(config, identity)\\n    run_dir = root / \\\"results\\\" / identifier\\n    _prepare_run_dir(run_dir, identity, force)\\n\\n    (run_dir / \\\"config.json\\\").write_bytes(canonical_json(config.as_dict()) + b\\\"\\\\n\\\")\\n    env = _environment(identity)\\n    (run_dir / \\\"env.json\\\").write_bytes(canonical_json(env) + b\\\"\\\\n\\\")\\n    if config.task == \\\"copy\\\":\\n        losses, learning_rates = _train(config)\\n        with (run_dir / \\\"metrics.jsonl\\\").open(\\\"w\\\", encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\") as handle:\\n            for step, (loss, lr) in enumerate(\\n                zip(losses, learning_rates, strict=True)\\n            ):\\n                handle.write(\\n                    json.dumps({\\\"step\\\": step, \\\"loss\\\": loss, \\\"lr\\\": lr}) + \\\"\\\\n\\\"\\n                )\\n        (run_dir / \\\"DONE\\\").touch()\\n        return run_dir\\n\\n    with (run_dir / \\\"metrics.jsonl\\\").open(\\\"w\\\", encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\") as handle:\\n        def record(step: int, loss: float, lr: float) -> None:\\n            handle.write(json.dumps({\\\"step\\\": step, \\\"loss\\\": loss, \\\"lr\\\": lr}) + \\\"\\\\n\\\")\\n            handle.flush()\\n\\n        model, _ = train_model(config, on_step=record)\\n    if config.variant in {\\\"m1\\\", \\\"m1b\\\"}:\\n        assert_stable(model)\\n    checkpoint = run_dir / \\\"final.pt\\\"\\n    torch.save({\\\"step\\\": config.steps, \\\"model\\\": model.state_dict()}, checkpoint)\\n    from stencil.evaluate import evaluate_model  # Avoid an entrypoint cycle.\\n\\n    result = evaluate_model(model, config)\\n    (run_dir / \\\"eval.json\\\").write_bytes(canonical_json(result) + b\\\"\\\\n\\\")\\n    (run_dir / \\\"DONE\\\").touch()\\n    return run_dir\\n\\n\\ndef _prepare_run_dir(\\n    run_dir: Path, identity: GitIdentity, force: bool\\n) -> None:\\n    if run_dir.exists():\\n        if not force:\\n            raise FileExistsError(f\\\"run directory already exists: {run_dir}\\\")\\n        env_path = run_dir / \\\"env.json\\\"\\n        try:\\n            prior = json.loads(env_path.read_text(encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\"))\\n        except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:\\n\\\"\\\"\\\"Shared base transformer and Phase 2 model-variant assembly.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\nfrom __future__ import annotations\\n\\nfrom collections import OrderedDict\\n\\nimport torch\\nfrom torch import nn\\nfrom torch.nn import functional as F\\n\\nfrom stencil.config import Config\\nfrom stencil.determinism import named_generator\\nfrom stencil.gates import apply_headwise_gate, project_b1_gate, project_control_gate\\nfrom stencil.oscillator import CueLatch, DecayCell, OscillatorController\\n\\n\\nclass Attention(nn.Module):\\n    def __init__(self, config: Config, layer_index: int) -> None:\\n        super().__init__()\\n        self.d_model = config.d_model\\n        self.n_heads = config.n_heads\\n        if config.d_model % config.n_heads:\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"d_model must be divisible by n_heads\\\")\\n        self.head_dim = config.d_model // config.n_heads\\n        if self.head_dim % 2:\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"RoPE head dimension must be even\\\")\\n        self.window = None if config.variant == \\\"b0_full\\\" else config.window\\n        self._use_banded = self.window is not None\\n        self._banded_block_size = None if self.window is None else 8 * self.window\\n        self.rope_theta = config.rope_theta\\n        self.layer_index = layer_index\\n        self.q = nn.Linear(config.d_model, config.d_model, bias=False)\\n        self.k = nn.Linear(config.d_model, config.d_model, bias=False)\\n        self.v = nn.Linear(config.d_model, config.d_model, bias=False)\\n        self.o = nn.Linear(config.d_model, config.d_model, bias=False)\\n\\n    def _rope(self, value: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:\\n        length = value.shape[2]\\n        frequency = self.rope_theta ** (\\n            -torch.arange(0, self.head_dim, 2, device=value.device, dtype=value.dtype)\\n            / self.head_dim\\n        )\\n        angle = (\\n            torch.arange(length, device=value.device, dtype=value.dtype)[:, None]\\n            * frequency[None]\\n        )\\n        cosine = angle.cos()[None, None]\\n        sine = angle.sin()[None, None]\\n        even, odd = value[..., 0::2], value[..., 1::2]\\n        return torch.stack(\\n            (even * cosine - odd * sine, even * sine + odd * cosine), dim=-1\\n        ).flatten(-2)\\n\\n    def _banded_layout(\\n        self,\\n        length: int,\\n        cue_mask: torch.Tensor | None,\\n        device: torch.device,\\n    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"Return gathered key positions and their validity mask.\\n\\n        Positions within each row are ordered as old global cues followed by\\n        the chronological local window.  A cue already in the local window is\\n        excluded from the global portion, so every allowed key occurs once.\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        assert self.window is not None\\n        queries = torch.arange(length, device=device)\\n        local_positions = (\\n            queries[:, None] + torch.arange(1 - self.window, 1, device=device)[None]\\n        )\\n        local_valid = local_positions >= 0\\n        local_positions = local_positions.clamp_min(0)\\n        if cue_mask is None:\\n            return local_positions[None], local_valid[None]\\n\\n        max_cues = int(cue_mask.sum(dim=1).max().item())\\n        if max_cues:\\n            all_positions = queries[None].expand(cue_mask.shape[0], -1)\\n            global_positions = torch.where(cue_mask, all_positions, length)\\n            global_positions = global_positions.sort(dim=1).values[:, :max_cues]\\n            global_positions = global_positions[:, None].expand(-1, length, -1)\\n            global_valid = global_positions <= queries[None, :, None] - self.window\\n            global_positions = global_positions.clamp_max(length - 1)\\n        else:\\n            global_positions = queries.new_empty(cue_mask.shape[0], length, 0)\\n            global_valid = cue_mask.new_empty(cue_mask.shape[0], length, 0)\\n        batch = cue_mask.shape[0]\\n        return (\\n            torch.cat(\\n                (global_positions, local_positions[None].expand(batch, -1, -1)),\\n                dim=-1,\\n            ),\\n            torch.cat(\\n                (global_valid, local_valid[None].expand(batch, -1, -1)),\\n                dim=-1,\\n            ),\\n        )\\n\\n    def _forward_banded(\\n        self,\\n        q: torch.Tensor,\\n        k: torch.Tensor,\\n        v: torch.Tensor,\\n        cue_mask: torch.Tensor | None,\\n    ) -> torch.Tensor:\\n        \\\"\\\"\\\"Compute exact causal-window attention in O(T * (window + cues)).\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n        assert self.window is not None\\n        batch, _, length, _ = q.shape\\n        queries = torch.arange(length, device=q.device)\\n        global_k = None\\n        global_v = None\\n        global_positions = None\\n        if cue_mask is not None:\\n            max_cues = int(cue_mask.sum(dim=1).max().item())\\n            if max_cues:\\n                all_positions = queries[None].expand(batch, -1)\\n                global_positions = torch.where(cue_mask, all_positions, length)\\n                global_positions = global_positions.sort(dim=1).values[:, :max_cues]\\n                gather_positions = global_positions.clamp_max(length - 1)\\n                gather_index = gather_positions[:, None, :, None].expand(\\n                    -1, self.n_heads, -1, self.head_dim\\n                )\\n                global_k = torch.gather(k, 2, gather_index)\\n                global_v = torch.gather(v, 2, gather_index)\\n\\n        chunks: list[torch.Tensor] = []\\n        assert self._banded_block_size is not None\\n        query_block = self._banded_block_size\\n        for start in range(0, length, query_block):\\n            end = min(start + query_block, length)\\n            key_start = max(0, start - self.window + 1)\\n            query_positions = queries[start:end]\\n            local_positions = queries[key_start:end]\\n            lag = query_positions[:, None] - local_positions[None]\\n            local_valid = (lag >= 0) & (lag < self.window)\\n            block_k = k[:, :, key_start:end]\\n            block_v = v[:, :, key_start:end]\\n\\n            if global_positions is not None:\\n                assert global_k is not None and global_v is not None\\n                global_valid = (\\n                    global_positions[:, None]\\n                    <= query_positions[None, :, None] - self.window\\n                )\\n                valid = torch.cat(\\n                    (\\n                        global_valid,\\n                        local_valid[None].expand(batch, -1, -1),\\n                    ),\\n                    dim=-1,\\n                )\\n                block_k = torch.cat((global_k, block_k), dim=2)\\n                block_v = torch.cat((global_v, block_v), dim=2)\\n            else:\\n                valid = local_valid\\n\\n            chunks.append(\\n                F.scaled_dot_product_attention(\\n                    q[:, :, start:end],\\n                    block_k,\\n                    block_v,\\n                    attn_mask=valid[:, None] if valid.ndim == 3 else valid,\\n                )\\n            )\\n        return torch.cat(chunks, dim=2)\\n\\n    def forward(\\n        self,\\n        x: torch.Tensor,\\n        gates: torch.Tensor | None,\\n        cue_mask: torch.Tensor | None = None,\\n        *,\\n        use_banded: bool | None = None,\\n    ) -> torch.Tensor:\\n        batch, length, _ = x.shape\\n\\n        def reshape(value: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:\\n            return value.view(batch, length, self.n_heads, self.head_dim).transpose(\\n                1, 2\\n            )\\n\\n        q = self._rope(reshape(self.q(x)))\\n        k = self._rope(reshape(self.k(x)))\\n        v = reshape(self.v(x))\\n        if cue_mask is not None and (\\n            cue_mask.shape != (batch, length) or cue_mask.dtype != torch.bool\\n        ):\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"cue_mask must be boolean with shape (batch, length)\\\")\\n        if use_banded is None:\\n            use_banded = self._use_banded\\n        if use_banded and self.window is not None:\\n            heads = self._forward_banded(q, k, v, cue_mask)\\n        else:\\n            positions = torch.arange(length, device=x.device)\\n            lag = positions[:, None] - positions[None, :]\\n            mask = lag >= 0\\n            if self.window is not None:\\n                local = lag < self.window\\n                if cue_mask is not None:\\n                    if (\\n                        cue_mask.shape != (batch, length)\\n                        or cue_mask.dtype != torch.bool\\n                    ):\\n                        raise ValueError(\\n                            \\\"cue_mask must be boolean with shape (batch, length)\\\"\\n                        )\\n                    mask = mask[None, None] & (\\n                        local[None, None] | cue_mask[:, None, None, :]\\n                    )\\n                else:\\n                    mask = mask & local\\n            heads = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, attn_mask=mask)\\n        if gates is not None:\\n            heads = apply_headwise_gate(heads, gates)\\n        merged = heads.transpose(1, 2).contiguous().view(batch, length, self.d_model)\\n        return self.o(merged)\\n\\n\\nclass Block(nn.Module):\\n    def __init__(self, config: Config, layer_index: int) -> None:\\n        super().__init__()\\n        self.attention_norm = nn.LayerNorm(config.d_model, eps=1e-5)\\n        self.attention = Attention(config, layer_index)\\n        self.mlp_norm = nn.LayerNorm(config.d_model, eps=1e-5)\\n        self.up = nn.Linear(config.d_model, config.d_ff, bias=False)\\n        self.down = nn.Linear(config.d_ff, config.d_model, bias=False)\\n\\n    def forward(\\n        self,\\n        x: torch.Tensor,\\n        gates: torch.Tensor | None,\\n        cue_mask: torch.Tensor | None = None,\\n    ) -> torch.Tensor:\\n        x = x + self.attention(self.attention_norm(x), gates, cue_mask)\\n        x = x + self.down(F.gelu(self.up(self.mlp_norm(x))))\\n        return x\\n\\n\\nclass StencilTransformer(nn.Module):\\n    \\\"\\\"\\\"One shared decoder-only transformer assembled into all eight variants.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n\\n    def __init__(self, config: Config) -> None:\\n        super().__init__()\\n        if config.variant not in {\\n            \\\"b0_full\\\",\\n            \\\"b0_local\\\",\\n            \\\"b1\\\",\\n            \\\"b2\\\",\\n            \\\"m1\\\",\\n            \\\"m1b\\\",\\n            \\\"b3\\\",\\n            \\\"b4\\\",\\n        }:\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"unknown model variant\\\")\\n        self.config = config\\n        self.token_embedding = nn.Embedding(config.vocab, config.d_model)\\n        self.blocks = nn.ModuleList(\\n            [Block(config, index) for index in range(config.n_layers)]\\n        )\\n        self.final_norm = nn.LayerNorm(config.d_model, eps=1e-5)\\n        self.lm_head = nn.Linear(config.d_model, config.vocab, bias=False)\\n\\n        generator = named_generator(config.seed_init, \\\"init\\\")\\n        self._initialize_base(generator)\\n        pathway_generator = named_generator(config.seed_init, \\\"pathway\\\")\\n        self.controller: nn.Module | None = None\\n        self.gate_weight: nn.Parameter | None = None\\n        self.gate_bias: nn.Parameter | None = None\\n        self.b1_weight: nn.Parameter | None = None\\n        if config.variant in {\\\"m1\\\", \\\"m1b\\\"}:\\n            self.controller = OscillatorController(config, pathway_generator)\\n        elif config.variant == \\\"b2\\\":\\n            self.controller = DecayCell(\\n                config.d_model, 128, generator=pathway_generator\\n            )\\n        elif config.variant == \\\"b3\\\":\\n            self.controller = CueLatch(config.d_model, 128, generator=pathway_generator)\\n        if config.variant in {\\\"m1\\\", \\\"m1b\\\", \\\"b2\\\", \\\"b3\\\"}:\\n            self.gate_weight = nn.Parameter(\\n                torch.empty(config.n_layers, config.n_heads, 128)\\n            )\\n            self.gate_bias = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(config.n_layers, config.n_heads))\\n            nn.init.normal_(\\n                self.gate_weight,\\n                mean=0.0,\\n                std=1e-3,\\n                generator=pathway_generator,\\n            )\\n        elif config.variant == \\\"b1\\\":\\n            self.b1_weight = nn.Parameter(\\n                torch.empty(config.n_layers, config.n_heads, config.d_model)\\n            )\\n            nn.init.normal_(\\n                self.b1_weight,\\n                mean=0.0,\\n                std=0.02,\\n                generator=pathway_generator,\\n            )\\n\\n    def _initialize_base(self, generator: torch.Generator) -> None:\\n        nn.init.normal_(\\n            self.token_embedding.weight, mean=0.0, std=0.02, generator=generator\\n        )\\n        for block in self.blocks:\\n            for linear in (\\n                block.attention.q,\\n                block.attention.k,\\n                block.attention.v,\\n                block.attention.o,\\n                block.up,\\n                block.down,\\n            ):\\n                nn.init.normal_(linear.weight, mean=0.0, std=0.02, generator=generator)\\n            nn.init.ones_(block.attention_norm.weight)\\n            nn.init.zeros_(block.attention_norm.bias)\\n            nn.init.ones_(block.mlp_norm.weight)\\n            nn.init.zeros_(block.mlp_norm.bias)\\n        nn.init.ones_(self.final_norm.weight)\\n        nn.init.zeros_(self.final_norm.bias)\\n        nn.init.normal_(self.lm_head.weight, mean=0.0, std=0.02, generator=generator)\\n\\n    def receptive_field(self) -> int:\\n        return self.config.n_layers * (self.config.window - 1)\\n\\n    def forward(\\n        self, tokens: torch.Tensor, *, gate_identity: bool = False\\n    ) -> torch.Tensor:\\n        return self.forward_embeddings(\\n            self.token_embedding(tokens),\\n            gate_identity=gate_identity,\\n            cue_mask=(tokens >= 1) & (tokens <= 32),\\n        )\\n\\n    def forward_embeddings(\\n        self,\\n        embeddings: torch.Tensor,\\n        *,\\n        gate_identity: bool = False,\\n        cue_mask: torch.Tensor | None = None,\\n    ) -> torch.Tensor:\\n        if gate_identity and self.config.variant in {\\\"b0_full\\\", \\\"b0_local\\\"}:\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"baseline has no gate to bypass\\\")\\n        control = None\\n        if self.config.variant == \\\"b3\\\":\\n            if cue_mask is None:\\n                raise ValueError(\\\"b3 embedding forwards require a cue_mask\\\")\\n            assert isinstance(self.controller, CueLatch)\\n            control = self.controller(embeddings, cue_mask)\\n        elif self.controller is not None:\\n            control = self.controller(embeddings)\\n        if self.config.variant == \\\"b4\\\" and cue_mask is None:\\n            raise ValueError(\\\"b4 embedding forwards require a cue_mask\\\")\\n        x = embeddings\\n        for layer_index, block in enumerate(self.blocks):\\n            normalized = block.attention_norm(x)\\n            gates = None\\n            if self.config.variant == \\\"b1\\\":\\n                if gate_identity:\\n                    gates = x.new_ones(x.shape[0], x.shape[1], self.config.n_heads)\\n                else:\\n                    assert self.b1_weight is not None\\n                    gates = project_b1_gate(normalized, self.b1_weight[layer_index])\\n            elif self.gate_weight is not None:\\n                if gate_identity:\\n                    gates = x.new_ones(x.shape[0], x.shape[1], self.config.n_heads)\\n                else:\\n                    assert control is not None and self.gate_bias is not None\\n                    gates = project_control_gate(\\n                        control,\\n                        self.gate_weight[layer_index],\\n                        self.gate_bias[layer_index],\\n                    )\\n            attention_cue_mask = cue_mask if self.config.variant == \\\"b4\\\" else None\\n            x = x + block.attention(normalized, gates, attention_cue_mask)\\n            x = x + block.down(F.gelu(block.up(block.mlp_norm(x))))\\n        return self.lm_head(self.final_norm(x))\\n\\n\\ndef count_params(module: nn.Module) -> int:\\n    return sum(\\n        parameter.numel()\\n        for parameter in module.parameters()\\n        if parameter.requires_grad\\n    )\\n\\n\\ndef _config_param_count(config: Config) -> int:\\n    d = config.d_model\\n    base = (\\n        2 * config.vocab * d\\n        + config.n_layers * (4 * d * d + 2 * d * config.d_ff + 4 * d)\\n        + 2 * d\\n    )\\n    gates = config.n_layers * config.n_heads * (128 + 1)\\n    if config.variant == \\\"b1\\\":\\n        return base + config.n_layers * config.n_heads * d\\n    if config.variant == \\\"b2\\\":\\n        return base + 128 * d + 128 + gates\\n    if config.variant == \\\"b3\\\":\\n        return base + 128 * d + gates\\n    if config.variant in {\\\"m1\\\", \\\"m1b\\\"}:\\n        assert config.osc_pairs is not None\\n        m = config.osc_pairs\\n        pathway = m * d + 3 * m * m + 2 * m + gates\\n        if config.variant == \\\"m1b\\\":\\n            pathway += 2 * m\\n        return base + pathway\\n    return base\\n\\n\\ndef _base_config(variant: str, d_ff: int, seed_init: int) -> Config:\\n    oscillatory = variant in {\\\"m1\\\", \\\"m1b\\\"}\\n    return Config(\\n        seed_data=0,\\n        seed_init=seed_init,\\n        seed_train=0,\\n        variant=variant,\\n        d_model=256,\\n        n_layers=4,\\n        n_heads=4,\\n        d_ff=d_ff,\\n        window=64,\\n
