References to \\\"Section 2b\\\" anywhere in this repo mean this file; \\\"this file\\\" in inherited text means the governed plan (PLAN.md plus this protocol). PLAN.md governs the science; this file governs how agents execute and review it.\\n\\n## 2b. Execution toolchain and adversarial review protocol (added v1.3)\\n\\nRoles, fixed:\\n\\n- Orchestrator: the Claude Code session driving this plan. It decomposes phases into work units, writes briefs, launches sol, verifies review findings, resolves what must be resolved, maintains this file's ledger, and makes gate/commit decisions. It does not write implementation code directly.\\n- Coder: the Codex CLI (`codex exec`) running model `gpt-5.6-sol` at `model_reasoning_effort=medium`, invoked via `tools/run_codex_agent.sh` with a brief in `tools/codex-agents/<name>.md`. Writes all implementation code and tests, following TDD per rule 1.\\n- Reviewer: the same model at `model_reasoning_effort=xhigh`, invoked via `tools/run_codex_review.sh <phase> <topic> <threshold>`. Performs adversarial review of the work, scored 0 to 100, writing to `plan/reviews/<phase>/<topic>.md`.\\n\\nReview protocol:\\n\\n1. Every review is adversarial: the reviewer's job is to break the work, not to bless it. Findings are graded low / medium / high / critical.\\n2. Context carry-over: each review round's prompt includes the prior rounds' full review file verbatim (the wrapper does this), so the reviewer always sees what it previously found, what was claimed fixed, and scores the delta. Round history is append-only in exactly this enforced sense (aligned v1.7): round headings and their recorded Score lines are immutable, high/critical findings may be closed with markers but never vanish, and any other change to prior content MUST carry a dated `(updated ...)` annotation — unannotated silent edits are a protocol violation the next round's reviewer is instructed to flag. `tools/review_round_tracking.py` enforces the mechanical invariants; the annotation duty binds the reviewer.\\n3. Finding identity and closure: a finding's identity is `<topic>#<number>` and its number is stable across rounds. The orchestrator independently verifies every high and critical finding (reads the code, reruns the test, or reproduces the claim), then either fixes it or prepares a refutation with evidence. Closure requires reviewer concurrence: only a subsequent reviewer round may mark a finding `(resolved ...)` or `(refuted ...)` after checking the fix or the refutation evidence itself; the orchestrator never edits reviewer-authored review files. `tools/check_review_scores.py` treats any unmarked high/critical finding as open and fails regardless of score. A human may override a deadlocked finding; the override is recorded in the ledger with rationale.\\n4. Resolution scope: fixes to implementation code and tests go through a coder brief (TDD per rule 1). Every coder brief MUST ship a scope allowlist `tools/codex-agents/<name>.allow` (glob patterns, one per line); the wrapper refuses to launch without one and hard-fails on out-of-scope diffs (mandatory per tie-break batch 2, 2026-08-22). A failed coder run's partial work is preserved as diagnostic evidence, never auto-reverted (same tie-break). Brief contract (v1.13, provenance v1.18): every brief states the objective, the allowlist, the tests to write first, the acceptance command, and the ledger handoff; the handoff entry MUST record the model, effort, wrapper log path, and codex session id actually used, and any CODEX_MODEL/CODEX_EFFORT override requires a ledgered reason. The orchestrator may directly edit only non-implementation files: PLAN.md, the plan/ working directory (PROTOCOL.md, LEDGER.md, AMENDMENTS.md), README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, configs, docs, and process tooling under tools/ (allowlist made explicit for the v1.17 split). Work is accepted only when zero high/critical findings remain open and the review score meets the threshold (default 90). Medium and low findings are recorded in the ledger and may be deferred with a stated reason.\\n5. Cadence: at minimum one review per phase before its exit commit. Lens selection, adaptive (v1.13, human directive): the orchestrator examines the work unit's actual diff and writes a purpose-built rubric fragment `tools/codex-prompts/review-<slug>.md`, where `<slug>` is the review's canonical topic identity: chosen once at first launch, recorded in the write-ahead entry, and reused verbatim for every later round of that review (v1.18) through whatever lens is most likely to break that change (numerical-analysis for cell math, distributional/leakage for generators, equivalence for refactors, claims-vs-evidence for writeups — or several fragments when the diff warrants); the chosen lens and rationale go in the write-ahead ledger entry, and lens adequacy is audited at retros against escaped defects. `review-phase.md` is the fallback when no bespoke lens is warranted, and the phase's kimi cross-review ALWAYS runs the generic `review-phase.md` lens regardless of bespoke sol lenses — the coverage backstop ensuring no diff is reviewed only through orchestrator-chosen lenses (v1.14). Known kimi coverage limits, disclosed rather than implied away (v1.18): kimi sees text artifacts only (no figures/binaries — their absence is stated in its context header) and oversized files are skipped with an explicit marker; amendments use `review-amendment.md`; retros use `review-retro.md` (kimi). Tie-breaks run via `tools/run_tiebreak.py` (prompt committed first, raw response preserved). One review (one canonical file, whatever its lens) still holds one reviewer session across its rounds. Topic manifest (v1.22, closes process#36): each phase's registered reviews live in `plan/reviews/<phase>/topics.txt`, one topic per line, a line reading `<topic> kimi` when a kimi companion (`<topic>-kimi.md`) is required; the manifest is written in the phase's first write-ahead entry and thereafter append-only; both wrappers refuse a topic absent from an existing manifest, and acceptance validates codex files against it and requires every flagged kimi companion. Required gate artifacts may be listed in `plan/reviews/<phase>/artifacts.txt`; the kimi context manifest reports each one present or absent, with byte size and sha256 for PRESENT rows; PRESENT rows for BINARY artifacts must additionally carry a prose description sufficient for content review — hash and size alone do not satisfy presentation — with enforcement binding at the first PRESENT binary row (batch-5 UPHOLD, 2026-08-22). Process #29 is deferred-open until that first row exists, not complete. Plus a review of any change to this file's governed content (hypotheses, thresholds, architecture). Plan-phase acceptance, defined (v1.12): the plan itself is accepted when `tools/check_acceptance.sh plan` passes — all sol plan topics at 90+ with zero open high/critical findings and kimi cross-reviews on file — after which Phase 0 may begin and further plan changes follow the amendment path. The gate's own tests (Appendix C) remain the scientific pass/fail authority; review scores gate code quality and cannot substitute for a green gate, and vice versa.\\n6. Gate acceptance checklist, all items required before a gate commit: (a) gate tests green (or the exact registered qualified state recorded), (b) the phase's sol review accepted, verified by `tools/check_acceptance.sh <phase>` (thresholds hardcoded at 90 inside the script — not parameterizable at invocation, v1.10), (c) the phase's kimi cross-review run before the commit with its confirmed high/critical findings resolved (v1.7), (d) ledger entry written, (e) README status row updated, (f) commit message names the gate state. No item may be waived by the agent.\\n7. The wrappers' file-write policy is mandatory: reviewers write only their canonical review file; coders write only what their brief scopes. Uncontained drift is a hard wrapper failure, not a warning. Wrapper runs are serialized per repo via `.review.lock`; never run a coder and a reviewer concurrently in this repo, and never edit repo files while a wrapper is running (its drift restorer will clobber the edits).\\n8. Budget discipline: before launching any multi-run matrix, run one pilot cell, record measured steps/sec and peak memory in the ledger, derive per-run and total wall-clock estimates, and set each run's timeout to 4x its pilot estimate. A matrix projected within 2x the phase's stated budget may launch with the projection recorded in the ledger; beyond 2x, pause for the human.\\n\\nPurpose-scoped review and stop-loss (v1.23, human ruling — Adjudication 3). THREAT MODEL, registered: agents are trusted-but-fallible; enforcement tooling detects mistakes and is NOT a defense against a malicious same-uid agent (unattainable per batch-2). Every review rubric states its purpose and threat model; findings outside them are out of scope. Stop-loss (round budget, v1.24, human ruling — Adjudication 4): every review has a budget of at most 10 rounds. A review reaching round 10 without acceptance triggers a kimi tie-break on one enumerated question — CONTINUE (further rounds are likely to reach acceptance on the existing findings) or STOP — with the review file's full round history inlined VERBATIM (summaries forbidden, per vacated batch 4) and the prompt committed pre-execution per the tie-break rules. On CONTINUE the budget extends to 15 rounds, an absolute ceiling; on STOP, or on exhausting round 15, the orchestrator decides against the north star (score advisory). Early exit retained from v1.23: ANY review at 3+ rounds with zero open high/criticals is decided by the orchestrator against the north star (score advisory). This supersedes v1.23's one-round cap for tooling-only changes. The 90-bar remains binding only for phase gates on the science.\\n\\nCross-model review, kimi (v1.6). kimi-k3 (`kimi-k3:cloud` via the local ollama daemon) is the second, independent reviewer: `python3 tools/run_kimi_review.py <phase> <topic> <threshold>` writes `plan/reviews/<phase>/<topic>-kimi.md` under the same round-log, append-only, and severity contracts, serialized on the same lock. Cadence: at least one kimi cross-review per phase on the gate-critical work, plus each retrospective (threshold 75 there). kimi is advisory — sol remains reviewer of record and kimi acceptance is not required for gates — but the orchestrator verifies kimi's high/critical claims and injects confirmed ones into sol's next round for adjudication; a confirmed, unrefuted kimi finding must be resolved like any other. Tie-break: when the orchestrator and sol deadlock on a finding after two full resolve-or-refute round trips, kimi receives the finding text VERBATIM, the fix or refutation evidence, and both arguments verbatim (summaries are forbidden — the vacated batch 4 shows why), and renders a verdict; the verdict is executed and ledger-recorded. Trigger order, reconciled (v1.22): two deadlocked round trips → kimi tie-break; sol disputing an EXECUTED tie-break in its next round → human touchpoint; a second dispute after a human ruling is out of scope for review. Mandatory human touchpoint (1) of the Autonomy policy now triggers only if sol's next round disputes the executed tie-break.\\n\\nReview-session continuity (v1.6). One review (one phase/topic file) is served by ONE reviewer session across all of its rounds: round 1 records the codex thread id (plan/reviews/.sessions/, machine-local, gitignored) and every later round resumes it, so the reviewer keeps its original context and re-verifies its own findings against the diffs instead of re-litigating from scratch. Anti-churn rule, binding on reviewers: rounds after the first re-examine existing findings and the changes; new findings are added only for regressions introduced by fixes or clear in-scope misses from the original review — scope never expands round-over-round. A new review (next phase or topic) starts a fresh session and then holds it for its own rounds. If a stored session is unusable, the wrapper falls back to a fresh run carrying the prior review file, noted in the wrapper log; the orchestrator MUST append the continuity-loss note to plan/LEDGER.md in the same working session (v1.18 — the log alone is not the audit record). kimi is stateless; its continuity is the prior rounds inlined in each call plus the same anti-churn rule.\\n\\nPhase retrospectives and agent evals (v1.6). After each phase's exit commit, before the next phase starts, the orchestrator writes `plan/retros/<phase>.md`: what went well and what went poorly, with evidence (finding counts and severities per round, fix attempts, reruns, wrapper failures, wall clock vs budget), root causes, and concrete optimizations. Every optimization lands as a diff in the retro commit — the AGENTS.md diff is quoted inside the retro document so the kimi retro review audits it (v1.19), an AGENTS.md entry (the agent playbook codex auto-loads and CLAUDE.md imports), a tooling or prompt fix under tools/, or a deferral ledgered with reason; changes to governed content still go through the amendment path. kimi reviews each retro (advisory, threshold 75) against one rubric question: does the retro assign blame where the evidence points. Performance is measured, not self-reported: `tools/agent_metrics.py` computes, from reviewer-authored review files and git history, first-round scores, rounds-to-acceptance, findings-per-round by severity, and open high/critical counts; the retro records the trend plus two hand-counted metrics, escaped defects (a finding whose root cause was accepted in an earlier phase) and lesson recurrence (a new finding matching an existing AGENTS.md lesson — the direct measure of whether the improvement loop works; target zero). Metrics are advisory and never gate science.\\n\\nAutonomy policy (v1.5). The project runs autonomously by default; honesty is enforced by the adversarial review protocol above and by the deterministic proof tests, not by human checkpoints. Concretely: wherever this plan says an amendment or decision is \\\"human-authorized,\\\" the autonomous path is that the orchestrator drafts the amendment with rationale, a sol@xhigh review of it is run (topic `amendment`, same wrapper), and it takes effect only once that review is accepted with zero open high/critical findings; the ledger records it and the human can audit asynchronously. Threshold freezes at first run launch remain absolute — no review can undo a freeze. Sequencing, auditable (v1.7, binding without exception since the v1.16 human ruling): an amendment's review must be accepted BEFORE the amendment commit lands — the reviewer reads the working-tree diff or draft, which the wrappers support (pre-existing dirty state is baseline, not drift); non-governed narrow commits (tie-break prompts, artifacts) go through `tools/commit_narrow.sh`, which stages only listed paths and refuses governed ones (v1.22, finding #12); amendment commits are made ONLY through `tools/amend.sh`, which takes the repo lock and refuses to commit unless the amendment review is ACCEPTED with its latest round quoting the current tree id from `tools/amend.sh --tree-id` (content binding: the reviewed tree IS the committed tree; any post-review edit changes the id and blocks the commit) and naming this version, the PLAN.md index line and plan/AMENDMENTS.md entry exist, and the topmost STATE line declares this amendment lands in this commit while naming the POST-commit next command (declared intent, v1.21 — committed STATE is fresh by construction) (v1.19, hardened v1.20 after the reviewer found the first version validated none of the review chain). Correction on the record (v1.20): Human Adjudication 2 made pre-commit review binding from that ruling forward; the orchestrator wrongly applied an extinguished initial-loop exception to v1.18 and v1.19 — both stand as committed, their substance reviewed post-hoc by rounds 16-17, and the violation is ledgered. Changes to acceptance tooling (check_review_scores.py, review_round_tracking.py, the wrappers), to reviewer/coder prompt fragments, or to AGENTS.md (behavioral instructions every agent loads; added v1.22 closing process#31) arising from retrospectives likewise take effect only after an amendment review accepts them (fragments added v1.13). Tie-break auditability (v1.13): every future tie-break's full prompt is committed verbatim to plan/tiebreaks/<phase>.md BEFORE the call executes. Ambiguities in this spec (old rule 7) are resolved autonomously by choosing the most conservative reading, recording the choice in the ledger, and flagging it for the next review round, rather than blocking on the human. The only mandatory human touchpoints are: (1) a review finding deadlocked after two full resolve-or-refute round trips, (2) a gate still red after three fix attempts (rule 4), (3) projected spend beyond 2x a phase budget, (4) renting external compute or any spending beyond this machine (Phase 7), and (5) anything destructive or outward-facing. Everything else proceeds without asking.\\n\\n\",\"exit_code\":1,\"status\":\"failed\"}}\n{\"type\":\"item.started\",\"item\":{\"id\":\"item_2\",\"type\":\"command_execution\",\"command\":\"/bin/bash -lc \\\"rg -n '\\\"'^STATE'\\\"' plan/LEDGER.md | head -n 3; sed -n '1,240p' plan/reviews/phase1/phase1.md; sed -n '1,240p' plan/reviews/phase1/phase1-kimi.md; sed -n '1,160p' phase1-fixes.allow\\\"\",\"aggregated_output\":\"\",\"exit_code\":null,\"status\":\"in_progress\"}}\n{\"type\":\"item.completed\",\"item\":{\"id\":\"item_2\",\"type\":\"command_execution\",\"command\":\"/bin/bash -lc \\\"rg -n '\\\"'^STATE'\\\"' plan/LEDGER.md | head -n 3; sed -n '1,240p' plan/reviews/phase1/phase1.md; sed -n '1,240p' plan/reviews/phase1/phase1-kimi.md; sed -n '1,160p' phase1-fixes.allow\\\"\",\"aggregated_output\":\"# Phase1 Review — phase1\\n\\n**Score:** 84 / 100\\n**Verdict:** CONDITIONAL PASS (75–89)\\n**Reviewer model:** codex/gpt-5.6-sol\\n**Date:** 2026-08-22\\n\\n## Round log\\n\\n### Round 1 — 2026-08-22 (codex/gpt-5.6-sol)\\n- Score: 84 / 100 (delta vs prior round: +84)\\n- Addressed since prior round:\\n  - Initial round; there are no prior findings to close.\\n  - Commit `68b9d92` committed the two fixtures before `src/stencil/data.py` or `tests/test_data.py` existed; commit `701833f` left both fixture hashes unchanged and added the implementation. The coder log records each of the nine named tests failing before its corresponding implementation and then passing.\\n  - Independent reconstruction from the registered seed derivation and draw order exactly matched both Latin rows, all four Task A fixture sequences, and all four Task M fixture sequences. The first Task A draws were cue 0, operand 1, distractors `[3, 1, 1, 4, 5, 2, 10, 0]`; the first Task M draws were keys `[20, 7, 13, 2]`, values `[7, 13, 10, 12]`, and query positions `[2, 1]`.\\n  - The current implementation matches the registered vocabulary, Latin-square construction, scalar draw sequences, causal masks, Task B cue switching, and strict beyond-window distance convention. Independent replay passed all 16 tests and Ruff; the worktree was clean before this review file was written.\\n- New or remaining:\\n  - README still reports Phase 1 as not started despite two ledger entries establishing that it was launched and its code landed.\\n  - The distractor-independence test samples cues itself and invokes an explicit-draw constructor, so it does not protect the production `task_a` sampling path on the registered grid.\\n  - `gate-1` does not generate or validate the required decoded-sample artifact.\\n  - The review launch does not record the required lens selection/rationale and uses the generic fallback despite this being a distribution-sensitive generator change.\\n  - Ruff excludes all of `tests/fixtures`, hiding the Phase 1 fixture-provenance Python program from the advertised repository lint check.\\n\\n## Findings\\n\\n1. **Medium — The governed status table never entered Phase 1.** `README.md:50` still says `not started`, while `plan/LEDGER.md:16` records the Phase 1 launch and `plan/LEDGER.md:13` records landed code. This violates the explicit state-transition rule at `PLAN.md:98` and the README's own explanation at `README.md:58`. The eventual green gate commit cannot retroactively make the required in-progress state truthful during the phase.\\n\\n2. **Medium — The distractor-independence regression guard bypasses the production Task A sampler.** `tests/test_data.py:90-110` creates its own `cues` generator and feeds a fixed list into `make_task_a_example`; it never calls `task_a` or `generate`. object\\\")\\n\\n    fields = {field.name for field in dataclasses.fields(Config)}\\n    unknown = set(raw) - fields\\n    if unknown:\\n        raise ValueError(f\\\"unknown config fields: {sorted(unknown)}\\\")\\n    try:\\n        config = Config(**raw)\\n    except TypeError as error:\\n        raise ValueError(f\\\"invalid config fields: {error}\\\") from error\\n    _validate(config)\\n    return config\\n\\n\\ndef _validate(config: Config) -> None:\\n    variants = {\\\"b0_full\\\", \\\"b0_local\\\", \\\"b1\\\", \\\"b2\\\", \\\"m1\\\", \\\"m1b\\\"}\\n    tasks = {\\\"a\\\", \\\"b\\\", \\\"m\\\", \\\"copy\\\"}\\n    if config.variant not in variants:\\n        raise ValueError(f\\\"invalid variant: {config.variant}\\\")\\n    if config.task not in tasks:\\n        raise ValueError(f\\\"invalid task: {config.task}\\\")\\n    if config.precision not in {\\\"fp32\\\", \\\"bf16\\\"}:\\n        raise ValueError(f\\\"invalid precision: {config.precision}\\\")\\n\\n    oscillatory = config.variant in {\\\"m1\\\", \\\"m1b\\\"}\\n    osc_fields = (\\n        config.osc_pairs,\\n        config.osc_cells,\\n        config.period_min,\\n        config.period_max,\\n        config.damping_learnable,\\n    )\\n    if oscillatory:\\n        if any(value is None for value in osc_fields):\\n            raise ValueError(\\n ValueError(\\\"damping_learnable is inconsistent with variant\\\")\\n        longest_delay = _longest_delay(config)\\n        if config.period_max is None or config.period_max < 2 * longest_delay:\\n \\\"task_delay_min\\\", \\\"task_delay_max\\\"},\\n        \\\"m\\\": {\\\"task_P\\\", \\\"task_queries\\\", \\\"task_placement\\\"},\\n        \\\"copy\\\": set(),\\n    }\\n    task_fields = {\\n        \\\"task_N\\\",\\n        \\\"task_k\\\",\\n        \\\"task_R\\\",\\n        \\\"task_delay_min\\\",\\n        \\\"task_delay_max\\\",\\n        \\\"task_P\\\",\\n        \\\"task_queries\\\",\\n        \\\"task_placement\\\",\\n    }\\n    required = required_by_task[config.task]\\n    missing = sorted(name for name in required if getattr(config, name) is None)\\n    inactive = sorted(\\n        name\\n        for name in task_fields - required\\n        if getattr(config, name) is not None\\n    )\\n    if missing:\\n        raise ValueError(f\\\"required task fields are null:     assert config.task_N is not None\\n        return config.task_N\\n    if config.task == \\\"b\\\":\\n        assert config.task_delay_max is not None\\n        return config.task_delay_max\\n    return config.context_len\\n\\n\\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\\nclass GitIdentity:\\n    git_sha: str\\n    git_diff_sha256: str\\n    untracked_sha256: str\\n    dirty: bool\\n\\n\\ndef git_identity(repo: str | Path = \\\".\\\") -> GitIdentity:\\n    root = Path(repo)\\n    git_sha = _git(root, \\\"rev-parse\\\", \\\"HEAD\\\").decode().strip()\\n    diff = _git(\\n        root,\\n        \\\"diff\\\",\\n        \\\"--binary\\\",\\n        \\\"--full-index\\\",\\n        \\\"--no-textconv\\\",\\n        \\\"--no-ext-diff\\\",\\n        \\\"HEAD\\\",\\n    )\\n    untracked_paths = _git(\\n        root, \\\"ls-files\\\", \\\"--others\\\", \\\"--exclude-standard\\\", \\\"-z\\\"\\n    ).split(b\\\"\\\\0\\\")\\n    records = bytearray()\\n    for encoded_path in sorted(path for path in untracked_paths if path):\\n        path = encoded_path.decode(\\\"utf-8\\\")\\n        file_path = root / path\\n        mode = file_path.lstat().st_mode\\n        if stat.S_ISLNK(mode):\\n            target = os.readlink(file_path).encode(\\\"utf-8\\\", \\\"surrogateescape\\\")\\n            content = (\\n                b\\\"L\\\\0\\\"\\n                + str(len(target)).encode(\\\"ascii\\\")\\n                + b\\\"\\\\0\\\"\\n                + target\\n            )\\n        else:\\n            content = file_path.read_bytes()\\n        records.extend(encoded_path)\\n        records.extend(b\\\"\\\\0\\\")\\n        records.extend(str(len(content)).encode(\\\"ascii\\\"))\\n        records.extend(b\\\"\\\\0\\\")\\n        records.extend(content)\\n    diff_hash = hashlib.sha256(diff).hexdigest()\\n    untracked_hash = hashlib.sha256(records).hexdigest()\\n    return GitIdentity(\\n        git_sha=git_sha,\\n )\\n    return hashlib.sha256(preimage).hexdigest()[:12]\\n\\n\\ndef _git(root: Path, *args: str) -> bytes:\\n    return subprocess.run(\\n        [\\\"git\\\", *args],\\n        cwd=root,\\n M1 and M1b are the same cell class and provably differ only in dissipation (M1's damping is a frozen zero buffer, M1b's is learnable; a bitwise test enforces that this is the only difference), so the M1 vs M1b comparison isolates dissipation cleanly. B2 is a separate architectural baseline from the first-order decay family — it differs in recurrence order, depth, and nonlinearity, not only in energy handling — and its results are read as \\\"what a simpler fading-memory architecture achieves,\\\" never as a third point on a controlled dissipation axis. Literature prior, stated in advance so the result reads honestly either way: D-LinOSS showed rigid dissipation limits representation and that forgetting is crucial for long-range reasoning, and Megalodon's damped complex rotation works at 7B, so the prior is M1b >= M1 >= B2 on the registered estimand. Decision rule, registered now (competence floor and uncertainty added v1.6): the primary estimand is mean exact-match accuracy over seeds {0,1,2} at Task A (2048, 32). The rule is evaluated only if the best OSCILLATORY variant's mean — max(mean(M1), mean(M1b)) — is >= 50 (v1.8; B2 cannot satisfy the floor, closing the path where the verdict adjudicates two failed oscillatory arms because the uncontrolled baseline happened to learn). The dissipation verdict adjudicates the M1b vs M1 gap ONLY (v1.7 — B2 is the uncontrolled architectural baseline and never enters the supported/refuted decision; the M1 vs B2 comparison is reported descriptively alongside): supported if mean(M1b) - mean(M1) >= 3 points AND >= 2x the pooled between-seed standard deviation `sqrt((var(M1b_seeds) + var(M1_seeds)) / 2)` (sample variances over the 3 seeds; registered heuristic, n = 3 acknowledged); refuted if reversed under the same two conditions; inconclusive otherwise. Task B's switching curves and stale-rule rates (Phase 5) are secondary descriptive evidence for the M1 vs M1b dissipation question only.\\n73:- H4 (channel use, claim-limiting). The 16 real-valued gates per position are NOT a proven information bottleneck — fp32 scalars at every position could in principle carry arbitrary content, and no capacity bound is claimed. H4 is therefore an empirical measurement of whether trained models in fact route content through the gates, operationalized by Task M. Interpretation is asymmetric by design, and detection is statistical, not a margin (v1.8): routing evidence EXISTS iff a registered one-sided exact binomial test rejects the 6.25 percent null at p < 0.001 for any seed. Trial definition (corrected v1.9 — a sequence-mean is not a Bernoulli trial): the FIRST queried answer of each eval sequence, correct or not; n = 10,000 exactly independent Bernoulli trials per seed with null p = 1/16. This discards the other seven answers for the existence decision (they still feed the magnitude bands), trading power for exactness; at a true 7.5 percent rate the test still rejects at ~5 sigma. Any detection forces the quantified-leakage subsection in REPORT.md and at least partial-separation wording of the Section 1 claim; the Appendix C bands then grade only the MAGNITUDE of detected routing. A non-detection is reported as \\\"no routing detected at the registered test,\\\" never as proof of purity.\\n145:    data.py                # task generators (Task A, Task B, Task M)\\n207:A stack of oscillatory state-space cells running left-to-right over the token embeddings, independent of the transformer's residual stream. Independence is deliberate. The control state is then a deterministic function of the input sequence alone, which makes causal patching in Phase 4 clean.\\n234:| frequency init | `sqrt(A)` log-spaced so periods span [period_min, period_max] = [8, 2 * longest task delay at this scale] (toy: [8, 4096]; Phase 6: [8, 16384]) |\\n242:The log-spaced period range must bracket every delay used in the tasks at the scale being trained, which is why period_max is parameterized rather than fixed. This is the \\\"slow control field\\\" claim made concrete. Frequencies are learned but initialized slow. The M1b damping init is deliberately near-conservative (retention over 2048 steps roughly 0.7 at init) so early training matches M1 and gradient descent discovers useful dissipation, which is the fair test of H2, rather than initializing M1b already forgetting.\\n286:- Rules are k fixed permutations of the 16-symbol operand alphabet, derived from `seed_rules` (v1.6 — a dedicated seed shared verbatim by the training and evaluation streams, so both use the identical rule table) with a Latin-rectangle construction. Registered sampler (v1.6, constructive — uniformity over all Latin squares is not needed, only column balance): start from the cyclic square `C[i][j] = (i + j) mod 16`; draw a row permutation σ, then a column permutation τ, then a symbol permutation π — three consecutive `torch.randperm(16)` calls on the `seed_rules` `rules` stream, in exactly that order (v1.10); the square is `L[i][j] = π(C[σ(i)][τ(j)])`. For k <= 16 the rules are its first k rows; for k = 32, two squares from independent draws stacked. Each row is a permutation, and for every operand `x` the k rule outputs are all distinct (k <= 16) or exactly balanced two-per-answer (k = 32). Exact functions, exact scoring.\\n288:- Sampling semantics, registered (v1.6; draw-call sequence v1.11): per sequence, in order — one `randint` on the `cues` stream (uniform over the k rules), one `randint` on the `operands` stream (uniform over 16), then N single `randint` draws on the `distractors` stream, one per distractor position. Mutually independent by stream construction, plus the frequency test below. Test asserts key-order independence and a registered known answer (v1.6): `canonical_json({\\\"b\\\": 2, \\\"a\\\": 1.5})` must be the bytes `{\\\"a\\\":1.5,\\\"b\\\":2}` and its sha256 must equal the value the orchestrator computes by hand with `python3 -c` and records in the test file before the hashing code exists (TDD-conform).\\n329:Tasks: repo layout, place the provided README.md at the repo root with every status row set to not started, `determinism.py`, config dataclass + hashing (the loader validates: unknown fields rejected, `damping_learnable` must be consistent with `variant`, task fields required iff the task uses them), minimal train loop on a dummy copy task, Makefile with `verify` and `gate-0`.\\n339:- `test_distractor_rule_independence` (frequency check described in Section 6: resample the rule assignment 10,000 times with distractors held fixed, assert each rule's frequency within 5 sigma of uniform)\\n343:- `test_task_m_bindings` (keys unique within a sequence, every query key appeared as a pair, answers match the binding; exact miniature fixture at P = 4 with 2 queries, `seed_rules = 0, seed_data = 0`, 4 sequences, authored under the same fixture-before-generator protocol as Task A; draw order per sequence: key permutation via one `randperm` on `keys`, P value `randint`s on `values`, query subset via one `randperm` on `queries` taking the first entries, v1.11)\\n415:Train M1, M1b, and B2 (seeds {0, 1, 2}) on Task B, R in {2, 8, 32}, with the Phase 3 training block and eval protocol unchanged (context sized to the longest R = 32 sequence). Phase 6 runs may not launch before that amendment lands.\\n443:## Appendix A. Config schema (single flat dataclass)\\n449:osc_pairs, osc_cells, period_min, period_max, damping_learnable\\n454:task_P, task_queries, task_placement     (m: in_window | beyond_window)\\n461:Loader validation (v1.4, v1.6): unknown fields rejected; for oscillatory variants `damping_learnable` must equal (`variant == m1b`), and for all other variants it is null like the rest of the osc_* block (v1.9 — the v1.8 wording made non-oscillatory configs unsatisfiable); task-specific fields required for the active task and must be null otherwise (task_k is active for tasks a and b); `osc_pairs`, `osc_cells`, `period_min`, `period_max`, `damping_learnable` must be null for non-oscillatory variants (v1.8); `period_max >= 2 * ` the task's longest delay for oscillatory variants. Phase 4/5 analysis settings (probe/patch/shuffle seeds and sizes) are fixed in this file's phase specs, not configurable. Test miniatures (for example Task M at P=4) override fields explicitly in test code. This schema covers Phases 0 through 5; Phase 6 adds its fields in its freeze amendment (that amendment must extend this appendix).\\n523:| NM-RNN (Costacurta et al., 2024), task-conditioned hypernetworks (von Oswald et al., 2019), HyperRNN (Ha et al., 2016), NeuMoSync (2026) | a slow neuromodulatory controller multiplicatively scaling a target network's weights, low-dimensional context switches framing | concept ancestors, RNN-era or continual-learning-focused, not oscillatory, not gating transformer attention, no necessity proof. NM-RNN reportedly forgets quickly under sequential training, worth citing when discussing Task B |\\n\\nSix variants. All share the base transformer code path. B0 variants are the same model class with the controller and gate modules ABSENT (not instantiated — no unused oscillator parameters exist in a B0 model; v1.6), not a separate model class. M1 and M1b must be the same cell class differing only in whether `G` is a frozen zero buffer or a parameter. B2 is a deliberately different architecture (first-order, no oscillation, no GLU stack) and is compared as such per H2's v1.4 wording. Init fairness note, B2's λ init moved from 0.99 to 0.999 in v1.1 so the variants with learnable dissipation (M1b, B2) start in a slow-forgetting regime and learn their forgetting rate; M1's dissipation is frozen at zero by design as the conservative pole.\\n\\n### 5.5 Parameter matching\\n\\nCounting rule: `count_params()` counts all trainable parameters (frozen buffers such as M1's `G` excluded, embeddings included). With the v1.4 shapes the additions are roughly: M1/M1b pathway ~31k (B_1 16384 + GLU 8192 + B_2 4096 + a_raw/g_raw 256 + gates 16 x 129 = 2064), B2 ~35k (B 32768 + λ 128 + gates 2064), B1 ~4k (16 x 256 gate vectors) — exact values come from code, not this paragraph. Matching procedure, registered (v1.6): M1 and M1b use the SAME config — identical `d_ff` (1024) and identical non-G initialization from the same seeds — so their contrast is exactly the dissipation parameter (the 128-parameter `g_raw` difference — two cells x 64, arithmetic corrected v1.7 — is inside tolerance by construction). The remaining variants widen `d_ff` in increments of 8 (deterministically: the smallest width matching the maximum-count variant within 1.0 percent) . The chosen `d_ff` per variant and the six exact counts are written to `results/params.md`, committed before the G2 commit and checked in the Phase 2 review, making the matching auditable rather than self-certified. A test asserts the match from the actual configs.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## 6. Task spec\\n\\nAll generators live in `data.py`, are pure functions of the config alone (the config carries every seed; v1.10), and yield `(tokens, loss_mask, metadata)`. Vocabulary is partitioned into disjoint ranges (Appendix B). Disjointness is asserted in tests.\\n\\nCausal alignment contract, fixed (v1.4). The model reads `tokens[0..T-1]`; `logits[p]` predicts `tokens[p+1]`. `loss_mask[p]` is true iff `tokens[p+1]` is an answer token, so the answer token itself is never an input to its own prediction. Training loss is cross-entropy of `logits[p]` vs `tokens[p+1]` at masked `p`; eval exact-match compares `argmax logits[p]` to `tokens[p+1]` at the same positions. The answer-decision position is `p` (the input position immediately before the answer token), and all cue distances and reachability assertions are measured to `p`. Miniature example, Task A with N=2: tokens `[cue, d, d, QRY, x, ans]` at positions 0..5; `loss_mask = [F, F, F, F, T, F]`; the model predicts `ans` from `logits[4]` (input `x`); cue distance is 4.\\n\\n### Task A. Cued rule application with delay\\n\\n```\\n[cue_i] [d_1 ... d_N] [QRY] [x] [answer = rule_i(x)]\\n```\\n\\n- Rules are k fixed permutations of the 16-symbol operand alphabet, derived from `seed_rules` (v1.6 — a dedicated seed shared verbatim by the training and evaluation streams, so both use the identical rule table) with a Latin-rectangle construction. Registered sampler (v1.6, constructive — uniformity over all Latin squares is not needed, only column balance): start from the cyclic square `C[i][j] = (i + j) mod 16`; draw a row permutation σ, then a column permutation τ, then a symbol permutation π — three consecutive `torch.randperm(16)` calls on the `seed_rules` `rules` stream, in exactly that order (v1.10); the square is `L[i][j] = π(C[σ(i)][τ(j)])`. For k <= 16 the rules are its first k rows; for k = 32, two squares from independent draws stacked. Each row is a permutation, and for every operand `x` the k rule outputs are all distinct (k <= 16) or exactly balanced two-per-answer (k = 32). Exact functions, exact scoring.\\n- Cue-blind null, exact by construction (v1.4). A model that sees `x` but not the cue faces k equiprobable, per-x-distinct (or balanced) answers, so its Bayes-optimal accuracy is exactly `1/k` for k <= 16 and exactly `1/16` for k = 32. The old flat \\\"chance = 6.25 percent\\\" claim was wrong for k < 16 and is retired. Per-cell nulls: k=2 -> 50%, k=8 -> 12.5%, k=32 -> 6.25%. `data.py` exposes `cue_blind_bayes(config)` returning this value, and G3.1 thresholds are null + 2 points per cell (Appendix C).\\n- Sampling semantics, registered (v1.6; draw-call sequence v1.11): per sequence, in order — one `randint` on the `cues` stream (uniform over the k rules), one `randint` on the `operands` stream (uniform over 16), then N single `randint` draws on the `distractors` stream, one per distractor position. Mutually independent by stream construction, plus the frequency test below. The committed Task A fixture is exactly 4 sequences at `seed_rules = 0, seed_data = 0` (k = 2, N = 8).\\n- Distractors are uniform over the distractor range, sampled independently of the rule. Zero mutual information with the rule by construction, asserted structurally (separate generator streams) and by a frequency test (rule resampled with distractors held fixed produces every rule with correct frequency).\\n- Grid: `N in {128, 512, 2048}`, `k in {2, 8, 32}`, where N counts distractor tokens; the cue-to-decision distance is N + 2 and unreachable placements assert distance > `receptive_field()` (Section 1 conventions). N = 128 is inside the receptive field (both B0s should solve it, sanity). N = 512 and N = 2048 exceed `L * w`.\\n\\n### Task B. Rule switching under interference\\n\\nR segments, each `[cue] [delay ~ U{32..256} distractor tokens] [QRY] [x] [answer]`, active rule is the most recent cue. R in {2, 8, 32}. Sampling semantics, fixed (v1.4, seed source corrected v1.7): k = 8 rules built with the Task A Latin-rectangle construction from `seed_rules` (shared train/eval, like Task A); each segment's cue is uniform over the 8 rules except that consecutive segments must differ (resample on repeat); operands uniform over the operand range, independent per segment. Metrics:\\n\\n- accuracy vs number of prior switches\\n- stale-rule error rate: over wrong answers at answer-decision positions, the fraction equal to `rule_j(x)` for at least one previously cued rule j of that sequence other than the active rule (counted once regardless of how many stale rules collide); reported as null when a cell has no wrong answers. This diagnostic separates failure modes. Conservation without overwrite predicts stale-rule error rates far above the guessing reference; decay predicts rates near it. Reference, registered (v1.7): the exact stale-match probability of a uniform-random wrong answer, computed analytically per sequence from the rule tables and metadata by `make_report.py` and drawn as the null line on every stale-rate plot.\\n\\n### Task M. MQAR anchor and channel-purity discriminator (added v1.1)\\n\\nFollows the Multi-Query Associative Recall structure of the Zoology line (Arora et al., 2023, github.com/HazyResearch/zoology), which is the canonical synthetic for recall in efficient architectures and correlates with language modeling performance. Adapted to this repo's fixed 64-token vocabulary and infinite-data regime (fresh sequences every step, a documented deviation from Zoology's fixed datasets).\\n\\n```\\n[k_1 v_1 k_2 v_2 ... k_P v_P] [gap] [QRY] [k_{q1}] [ans = v(k_{q1})] [k_{q2}] [ans] ...\\n```\\n\\n- Keys drawn without replacement from the 32-token cue range (reused as keys, cues do not appear in Task M); P = 32 uses every key each sequence, in random order. Values drawn with replacement, uniform over the 16-symbol operand range. 8 queried keys sampled without replacement uniformly from the 32 pairs, query order random. Chance = 6.25 percent (values are uniform and independent of the queried key, so the cue-blind and key-blind null really is 1/16 here).\\n- Two placements, each trained separately. In-window, gap = 0, pairs immediately precede queries, this is the literature-calibration cell. Beyond-window, gap = `model.receptive_field() + 64` uniform distractor tokens, which makes every pair's value token lie more than `receptive_field()` before every answer-decision position; the generator asserts the distance.\\n- Purpose one, calibration. B0-full at or above 95 on the in-window cell is a sanity requirement showing our MQAR implementation is learnable by full attention, the established paragon on this task. Because our cell deviates from Zoology's fixed-dataset regime (documented above), a miss triggers diagnosis — generator bug, optimization, or capacity — recorded in the ledger before any fix; it is not automatically an implementation deviation, and any fix beyond a diagnosed generator bug requires an amendment.\\n- Purpose two, H4 (claim-limiting, per the v1.4 hypothesis wording). Task M is content recall, not rule application. The beyond-window accuracy of M1 and M1b measures whether trained models route content through the gate pathway, with pre-registered interpretation bands in Appendix C. High accuracy forces withdrawal or qualification of the separation claim; low accuracy is \\\"no evidence of content routing,\\\" not proof of purity.\\n\\n### Loss and eval\\n\\nCross-entropy at masked answer-decision positions only, per the causal alignment contract above. Eval protocol, frozen (v1.4, seed split corrected v1.6): rule tables derive from `seed_rules` alone; example streams derive from `seed_data` (training) and `seed_data + eval_seed_offset` (evaluation). The two streams therefore share the identical rule table by construction while drawing disjoint example sequences — the v1.4 wording derived rules from the dataset seed, which would have silently evaluated against a different rule table. Evaluation uses 10,000 fresh sequences per cell from the eval stream, scored at the final checkpoint (step 20k) only — no best-checkpoint selection. Metric is exact-match accuracy pooled over all answer-decision positions; per-seed accuracy is reported, and every Appendix C bar names its seed aggregation explicitly (v1.6). Binomial 95 percent CI half-width at n = 10,000 is under 1 point at all relevant accuracies, comfortably inside the +2-point gate margins. The task tests rule application at delay, not rule generalization. Results are written per cell as JSON: `{cell, variant, seed, n_sequences, n_answers, accuracy}`.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Phase 0. Scaffold and determinism harness\\n\\nObjective. Empty repo to green determinism gate.\\n\\nTests first:\\n- `test_determinism_two_runs_bitwise`. Uses the committed `configs/test_tiny.json`, registered in full (v1.11): variant b0_local, d_model 64, L 2, H 2, d_ff 256, w 16, vocab 64, task `copy` — sequences of 64 tokens uniform over the operand range from the `operands` stream, target at each position = previous token, loss over positions 1 onward — batch 8, 200 steps, the Phase 3 optimizer block, fp32, all seeds 0, single device; trains twice in-process from identical seeds and asserts the two 200-entry loss sequences are bitwise identical.\\n- `test_config_hash_stable`. Config hashing is `sha256` of the canonical JSON encoding — keys sorted, separators `(\\\",\\\", \\\":\\\")`, floats via `repr` — of the full config dict, `run_id` per the Section 3 formula verbatim (the four-term v1.11 form with the framed untracked record; Section 3 is the sole authority and this sentence intentionally does not restate it). Test asserts key-order independence and a registered known answer (v1.6): `canonical_json({\\\"b\\\": 2, \\\"a\\\": 1.5})` must be the bytes `{\\\"a\\\":1.5,\\\"b\\\":2}` and its sha256 must equal the value the orchestrator computes by hand with `python3 -c` and records in the test file before the hashing code exists (TDD-conform).\\n- `test_seed_isolation`. Changing `seed_data` leaves the initial `state_dict` bytes identical and changes the first batch's token tensor; changing `seed_init` does the reverse.\\n\\nRun-directory policy (v1.4): `results/<run_id>/` is created fresh per run; if it already exists the trainer refuses to start unless `--force` is passed, and `--force` deletes and recreates the directory ONLY when its `env.json` records the same git state (aligned v1.9 with Section 3 — evidence from different code is never deleted by tooling). Metrics are never appended across invocations.\\n\\nTasks: repo layout, place the provided README.md at the repo root with every status row set to not started, `determinism.py`, config dataclass + hashing (the loader validates: unknown fields rejected, `damping_learnable` must be consistent with `variant`, task fields required iff the task uses them), minimal train loop on a dummy copy task, Makefile with `verify` and `gate-0`.\\n\\nGate G0: `make gate-0` runs the three tests plus ruff. Exit: green, commit.\\n\\n## Phase 1. Data generators\\n\\nTests first:\\n- `test_task_a_exact_output` (fixed seed, assert exact token sequences against committed fixture files for k=2, N=8 miniatures; TDD-conform protocol registered v1.6: the orchestrator hand-executes the registered constructions — cyclic-square sampler, sampling semantics, alignment contract — for `seed_rules=0, seed_data=0`, writes the expected sequences into the fixture BEFORE the generator is implemented, and the generator must then reproduce them exactly; any mismatch is adjudicated against the registered construction, never by regenerating the fixture)\\n- `test_rules_are_permutations` (bijectivity per rule)\\n- `test_vocab_ranges_disjoint`\\n- `test_distractor_rule_independence` (frequency check described in Section 6: resample the rule assignment 10,000 times with distractors held fixed, assert each rule's frequency within 5 sigma of uniform)\\n- `test_rules_latin_rectangle` (for each dataset seed tested: every row a permutation, every column of the k x 16 output table has distinct entries for k <= 16 and exactly-two-per-answer balance for k = 32, and `cue_blind_bayes(config)` returns exactly 1/k or 1/16 accordingly)\\n- `test_loss_mask_positions` (mask true exactly at answer-DECISION positions — the input positions whose logits predict answer tokens, per the Section 6 contract — all three tasks; wording corrected v1.6)\\n- `test_task_b_active_rule_tracking` (metadata's active-rule labels match most-recent-cue semantics on constructed cases)\\n- `test_task_m_bindings` (keys unique within a sequence, every query key appeared as a pair, answers match the binding; exact miniature fixture at P = 4 with 2 queries, `seed_rules = 0, seed_data = 0`, 4 sequences, authored under the same fixture-before-generator protocol as Task A; draw order per sequence: key permutation via one `randperm` on `keys`, P value `randint`s on `values`, query subset via one `randperm` on `queries` taking the first entries, v1.11)\\n- `test_task_m_gap_exceeds_receptive_field` (beyond-window placement's minimum pair-to-query distance strictly greater than `receptive_field()` from the model config it will be paired with)\\n\\nGate G1: all data tests green, plus a generated `results/data_samples.md` showing 3 decoded samples per task and placement for human eyeball. The Phase 1 review MUST include the reviewer's own hand-verification of the committed fixtures against the registered constructions, recorded in the review file (binding condition of the 2026-08-22 tie-break on spec#9, plan/tiebreaks/plan.md). Exit: green, commit.\\n\\n## Phase 2. Models and plumbing proofs\\n\\nTests first, in this order:\\n\\n1. `test_oscillator_matches_discrete_closed_form` (v1.4; cases registered v1.8; numerics fixed v1.11). Single oscillators at periods {8, 64, 4096}, each under zero forcing (initial state `y_0, z_0 ~ N(0,1)` from stream `fixtures:init`, nonzero by construction) and unit constant forcing (b = 1, u = 1, `y_0 = z_0 = 0`), G in {0, 1e-2}: the cell executed in fp64 must match the exact discrete solution (matrix power of the one-step map plus the forced particular solution, fp64) over 1000 steps at rtol 1e-9, atol 1e-12 — the old absolute 1e-5 was infeasible: unit forcing at period 4096 reaches ~4e5 amplitude, where fp32 ulps are ~3e-2. Separately, the fp32 cell must match the fp64 cell at rtol 1e-4, atol 1e-6 on the same cases (this pair, not the closed form, bounds production numerics). Every tolerance in Phase 2 is rtol/atol, stated explicitly. A separate non-gating analysis records the discrete-vs-continuous deviation versus dt for the report.\\n2. `test_discrete_invariant_conserved` (v1.4, fixtures instantiated v1.6, completed v1.13). Zero input, `y, z ~ N(0,1)` from stream `fixtures:init` seed 0, standard log-spaced `A`, G = 0: the registered discrete invariant `H_d` (Section 5.2) drifts less than rtol 1e-5 in fp64 and rtol 1e-3 in fp32 over 10k steps, and the continuous energy `H = z^2 + A y^2` stays bounded — max excursion below 4x its initial value — with no trend: window = 1000 steps, trend = least-squares slope over the last five window means, |slope| < 1e-6 x `H_0` per window (v1.13). `test_damped_energy_decays`, two registered G regimes (v1.6): (a) G = 1e-2 fixed: windowed 1k-step means strictly decreasing and `H_10000 < 1e-2 * H_0`; (b) G = softplus(-9) ~ 1.23e-4 (the registered M1b init): windowed means non-increasing and the `H_10000 / H_0` ratio within [0.8, 1.2] x `(1+G)^(-10000)` (~0.29; exponent corrected v1.7 — the v1.6 formula double-counted the per-step determinant; verify the exact modal decay analytically during implementation and record it in a code comment). `test_decay_ssm_energy_decays` for B2's cell: state dim 128, λ = 0.999, initial state N(0,1) from `fixtures:init` seed 0, zero input, 10k steps, windowed means non-increasing and final state-norm-squared ratio within [0.8, 1.2] x `λ^(2 * 10000)` (v1.13).\\n2b. `test_stability_bound` (v1.6). Asserts `dt * sqrt(A) < 2` elementwise for every oscillator at init, and provides the checkpoint assertion reused by the gates: every checkpoint entering G3/G4/G6 evidence must pass it (a violation makes that gate red — validity condition in Appendix C).\\n3. `test_damping_zero_matches_m1_bitwise`. Instantiate the unified cell as M1b, set the damping to exactly zero through the code path built for M1's frozen buffer (a `zero_damping` flag that bypasses `softplus`, since `softplus(g_raw)` can never be exactly 0 for finite `g_raw`), drive both with N(0,1) inputs (length 512, stream `fixtures:input` seed 0) from N(0,1) initial states (`fixtures:init`), assert outputs are nonzero and bitwise identical to the M1 configuration in fp32 (nonzero-input case registered v1.13 — a zero trajectory would pass vacuously). Sequential PyTorch cells reproduce the committed reference trajectories from the official JAX implementations at rtol 1e-5, atol 1e-8 (v1.13). Workflow per Appendix G.\\n5. `test_scan_equals_sequential`. Runs (and gates G2) only if a parallel scan implementation exists in the repo; it must match the sequential oracle at rtol 1e-5, atol 1e-8 on N(0,1) inputs of shape (batch 4, length 512, m 64), fp32, stream `fixtures:input` seed 0 (v1.13). Build M1 and B0-local from the same seed with shared-submodule init (the base transformer is constructed first from `seed_init` so both variants consume identical RNG streams for shared modules; pathway modules draw from a separate derived generator), force the gate multiplier to exactly 1.0 via a bypass flag (not by driving the sigmoid), and assert forward logits on one Task A batch (batch 8, the (512, 8) cell, `seed_rules = 0, seed_data = 0`, v1.13) are bitwise identical in fp32. B0-local, fp32, untrained models from seeds {0, 1, 2}, the first 3 eval-stream sequences from each unreachable cell (N = 512 and N = 2048; sample count and fixture identity registered v1.13). For every answer-decision position, compute the Jacobian of the full vocab logit vector with respect to the input-embedding activation at the cue position (the activation at that position, not the embedding table row). Assert every entry is exactly zero, and assert the gradient object is a real zero tensor, not `None` (a `None`/detached graph fails the test — it means the path was never connected, which would make the test vacuous). Repeat for B1. Then assert the same Jacobian is nonzero for M1, M1b, and B2 at the same placements. After Phase 3 training, rerun this test on the trained B0-local and B1 checkpoints as a regression guard. This is the load-bearing proof test.\\n8. `test_cue_reachable_when_close`. Same machinery with the cue placed so the cue-to-decision distance is exactly `receptive_field()` (reachable by one path): gradient nonzero for B0-local. Next after acceptance: `bash tools/check_acceptance.sh phase1`, gate(G1) commit flipping README Phase 1 row, `git push origin main`, then v1.25 amendment draft + review, then Phase 2 brief.\n    19\t\n    15\t1. Every review is adversarial: the reviewer's job is to break the work, not to bless it. Findings are graded low / medium / high / critical.\n    16\t2. Context carry-over: each review round's prompt includes the prior rounds' full review file verbatim (the wrapper does this), so the reviewer always sees what it previously found, what was claimed fixed, and scores the delta. Round history is append-only in exactly this enforced sense (aligned v1.7): round headings and their recorded Score lines are immutable, high/critical findings may be closed with markers but never vanish, and any other change to prior content MUST carry a dated `(updated ...)` annotation — unannotated silent edits are a protocol violation the next round's reviewer is instructed to flag. `tools/review_round_tracking.py` enforces the mechanical invariants; the annotation duty binds the reviewer.\n    17\t3. Finding identity and closure: a finding's identity is `<topic>#<number>` and its number is stable across rounds. The orchestrator independently verifies every high and critical finding (reads the code, reruns the test, or reproduces the claim), then either fixes it or prepares a refutation with evidence. Closure requires reviewer concurrence: only a subsequent reviewer round may mark a finding `(resolved ...)` or `(refuted ...)` after checking the fix or the refutation evidence itself; the orchestrator never edits reviewer-authored review files. `tools/check_review_scores.py` treats any unmarked high/critical finding as open and fails regardless of score. A human may override a deadlocked finding; the override is recorded in the ledger with rationale.\n    18\t4. Resolution scope: fixes to implementation code and tests go through a coder brief (TDD per rule 1). Every coder brief MUST ship a scope allowlist `tools/codex-agents/<name>.allow` (glob patterns, one per line); the wrapper refuses to launch without one and hard-fails on out-of-scope diffs (mandatory per tie-break batch 2, 2026-08-22). A failed coder run's partial work is preserved as diagnostic evidence, never auto-reverted (same tie-break). Brief contract (v1.13, provenance v1.18): every brief states the objective, the allowlist, the tests to write first, the acceptance command, and the ledger handoff; the handoff entry MUST record the model, effort, wrapper log path, and codex session id actually used, and any CODEX_MODEL/CODEX_EFFORT override requires a ledgered reason. The orchestrator may directly edit only non-implementation files: PLAN.md, the plan/ working directory (PROTOCOL.md, LEDGER.md, AMENDMENTS.md), README.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, configs, docs, and process tooling under tools/ (allowlist made explicit for the v1.17 split). Work is accepted only when zero high/critical findings remain open and the review score meets the threshold (default 90). Medium and low findings are recorded in the ledger and may be deferred with a stated reason.\n    19\t5. Cadence: at minimum one review per phase before its exit commit. Lens selection, adaptive (v1.13, human directive): the orchestrator examines the work unit's actual diff and writes a purpose-built rubric fragment `tools/codex-prompts/review-<slug>.md`, where `<slug>` is the review's canonical topic identity: chosen once at first launch, recorded in the write-ahead entry, and reused verbatim for every later round of that review (v1.18) through whatever lens is most likely to break that change (numerical-analysis for cell math, distributional/leakage for generators, equivalence for refactors, claims-vs-evidence for writeups — or several fragments when the diff warrants); the chosen lens and rationale go in the write-ahead ledger entry, and lens adequacy is audited at retros against escaped defects. `review-phase.md` is the fallback when no bespoke lens is warranted, and the phase's kimi cross-review ALWAYS runs the generic `review-phase.md` lens regardless of bespoke sol lenses — the coverage backstop ensuring no diff is reviewed only through orchestrator-chosen lenses (v1.14). Known kimi coverage limits, disclosed rather than implied away (v1.18): kimi sees text artifacts only (no figures/binaries — their absence is stated in its context header) and oversized files are skipped with an explicit marker; amendments use `review-amendment.md`; retros use `review-retro.md` (kimi). Tie-breaks run via `tools/run_tiebreak.py` (prompt committed first, raw response preserved). One review (one canonical file, whatever its lens) still holds one reviewer session across its rounds. Topic manifest (v1.22, closes process#36): each phase's registered reviews live in `plan/reviews/<phase>/topics.txt`, one topic per line, a line reading `<topic> kimi` when a kimi companion (`<topic>-kimi.md`) is required; the manifest is written in the phase's first write-ahead entry and thereafter append-only; both wrappers refuse a topic absent from an existing manifest, and acceptance validates codex files against it and requires every flagged kimi companion. Required gate artifacts may be listed in `plan/reviews/<phase>/artifacts.txt`; the kimi context manifest reports each one present or absent, with byte size and sha256 for PRESENT rows; PRESENT rows for BINARY artifacts must additionally carry a prose description sufficient for content review — hash and size alone do not satisfy presentation — with enforcement binding at the first PRESENT binary row (batch-5 UPHOLD, 2026-08-22). Process #29 is deferred-open until that first row exists, not complete. Plus a review of any change to this file's governed content (hypotheses, thresholds, architecture). Plan-phase acceptance, defined (v1.12): the plan itself is accepted when `tools/check_acceptance.sh plan` passes — all sol plan topics at 90+ with zero open high/critical findings and kimi cross-reviews on file — after which Phase 0 may begin and further plan changes follow the amendment path. The gate's own tests (Appendix C) remain the scientific pass/fail authority; review scores gate code quality and cannot substitute for a green gate, and vice versa.\n    20\t6. Gate acceptance checklist, all items required before a gate commit: (a) gate tests green (or the exact registered qualified state recorded), (b) the phase's sol review accepted, verified by `tools/check_acceptance.sh <phase>` (thresholds hardcoded at 90 inside the script — not parameterizable at invocation, v1.10), (c) the phase's kimi cross-review run before the commit with its confirmed high/critical findings resolved (v1.7), (d) ledger entry written, (e) README status row updated, (f) commit message names the gate state. No item may be waived by the agent.\n    21\t7. The wrappers' file-write policy is mandatory: reviewers write only their canonical review file; coders write only what their brief scopes. Uncontained drift is a hard wrapper failure, not a warning. Wrapper runs are serialized per repo via `.review.lock`; never run a coder and a reviewer concurrently in this repo, and never edit repo files while a wrapper is running (its drift restorer will clobber the edits).\n    22\t8. Budget discipline: before launching any multi-run matrix, run one pilot cell, record measured steps/sec and peak memory in the ledger, derive per-run and total wall-clock estimates, and set each run's timeout to 4x its pilot estimate. A matrix projected within 2x the phase's stated budget may launch with the projection recorded in the ledger; beyond 2x, pause for the human.\n    23\t\n    24\tPurpose-scoped review and stop-loss (v1.23, human ruling — Adjudication 3). THREAT MODEL, registered: agents are trusted-but-fallible; enforcement tooling detects mistakes and is NOT a defense against a malicious same-uid agent (unattainable per batch-2). Every review rubric states its purpose and threat model; findings outside them are out of scope. Stop-loss (round budget, v1.24, human ruling — Adjudication 4): every review has a budget of at most 10 rounds. A review reaching round 10 without acceptance triggers a kimi tie-break on one enumerated question — CONTINUE (further rounds are likely to reach acceptance on the existing findings) or STOP — with the review file's full round history inlined VERBATIM (summaries forbidden, per vacated batch 4) and the prompt committed pre-execution per the tie-break rules. On CONTINUE the budget extends to 15 rounds, an absolute ceiling; on STOP, or on exhausting round 15, the orchestrator decides against the north star (score advisory). Early exit retained from v1.23: ANY review at 3+ rounds with zero open high/criticals is decided by the orchestrator against the north star (score advisory). This supersedes v1.23's one-round cap for tooling-only changes. b_t = g_t * softmax(e_t) / max(softmax(e_t))   (peak-normalized A2:

attn_bias path.

        super().__init__()
        self.beta_max = beta_max
        self.W_q = torch.nn.Linear(2048, 64)
        self.W_k = torch.nn.Linear(2048, 64)
        self.w_g = torch.nn.Linear(2048, 1)
        torch.nn.init.zeros_(self.w_g.weight)
        torch.nn.init.constant_(self.w_g.bias, -2.0)

    def gain(self, h20):
        return self.beta_max * torch.sigmoid(self.w_g(h20)).squeeze(-1)

    def field(self, H, K):
        """H [T, 2048] generation states, K [P, 2048] prompt features
        -> peak-normalized bias field [T, P]."""
        q = F.normalize(self.W_q(H), dim=-1)
        k = F.normalize(self.W_k(K), dim=-1)
        e = 8.0 * (q @ k.T)
        sm = F.softmax(e, dim=-1)
        sm = sm / sm.max(dim=-1, keepdim=True).values
        return self.gain(H)[:, None] * sm

    def forward(self, h20, K):
        return self.field(h20[None], K)[0]


class WaveRNN(torch.nn.Module):
    """W1 recurrent wave (frozen contract v3 W1 + v3.1 H3):
    s_t = GRU(h20_t, s_{t-1}) FIRST, then q_t/g_t from [h20_t; s_t]
    (score-after-write). State 64-d; reset/detach are the trainer's
    responsibility. Field math identical to the A2 selection."""

    def __init__(self, beta_max: float = 2.0):
        super().__init__()
        self.beta_max = beta_max
        self.gru = torch.nn.GRUCell(2048, 64)
        self.W_q = torch.nn.Linear(2048 + 64, 64)
        self.W_k = torch.nn.Linear(2048, 64)
        self.w_g = torch.nn.Linear(2048 + 64, 1)
        torch.nn.init.zeros_(self.w_g.weight)
        torch.nn.init.constant_(self.w_g.bias, -2.0)

    def init_state(self):
        return torch.zeros(64)

    def step(self, h20, s_prev, K):
        """-> (bias row [P], s_t). Score from the JUST-UPDATED state."""
        s_t = self.gru(h20[None], s_prev[None])[0]
        x = torch.cat([h20, s_t])
        q = F.normalize(self.W_q(x), dim=-1)
        k = F.normalize(self.W_k(K), dim=-1)
        e = 8.0 * (q @ k.T)
        sm = F.softmax(e, dim=-1)
        sm = sm / sm.max()
        g = self.beta_max * torch.sigmoid(self.w_g(x)).squeeze(-1)
        return g * sm, s_t
# ruff: noqa: E501
"""BENCH-WAVE runner library (B0.3): IFEval loading, scoring, and the
single KV-cached greedy generator every arm uses.

Scoring wraps the vendored upstream verifiers (vendor/ifeval, from
lm-eval's pinned copy of Google's code) — strict + loose, four metrics.
langdetect's internal randomness is pinned at import. The single-use
invariant lives with the CALLERS: nothing here touches the 541 with a
model; sealed jobs do that once.
"""
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
if str(ROOT / "vendor") not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "vendor"))

import langdetect  # noqa: E402

langdetect.DetectorFactory.seed = 0

from ifeval import utils as ifeval_utils  # noqa: E402

TMPL = "<|im_start|>user\n{p}<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n<think>\n\n</think>\n\n"
EOS = {151645, 151643}
MAX_NEW = 1024  # registered candidate; frozen at checkpoint ii
WAVE_LAYERS = range(20, 28)


def load_ifeval(path):
    return [json.loads(line) for line in open(path)]


def score_response(row, response):
    """four booleans/lists for one prompt via the vendored upstream code.

    REGISTERED PIN: upstream build_description draws from the global
    `random` module when kwargs are invalid — in the 541 exactly two
    rows (keys 1122, 1129: letter_frequency with non-a-z letters) are
    random-state-sensitive. We seed per-row by key so scoring is a pure
    function of (row, response), order-independent."""
    import random
    random.seed(row["key"])
    return ifeval_utils.process_results(row, [response])


def aggregate(per_prompt):
    """the four registered IFEval metrics from per-prompt score dicts."""
    n = len(per_prompt)
    return {
        "prompt_level_strict_acc": sum(p["prompt_level_strict_acc"] for p in per_prompt) / n,
        "inst_level_strict_acc": ifeval_utils.agg_inst_level_acc(
            [p["inst_level_strict_acc"] for p in per_prompt]),
        "prompt_level_loose_acc": sum(p["prompt_level_loose_acc"] for p in per_prompt) / n,
        "inst_level_loose_acc": ifeval_utils.agg_inst_level_acc(
            [p["inst_level_loose_acc"] for p in per_prompt]),
    }


def generate_cached(m, tok, prompt, bias_fn=None, max_new=MAX_NEW, deadline_s=None):
    """THE generator for every arm: pinned template, KV-cached greedy,
    registered EOS/max_new. bias_fn(h20, prompt_len, past_len) -> bias
    tensor (t, past_len + t) or None, computed from the SAME forward's
    layer-20 input via a mid-forward hook (train/test same-position
    semantics; h20 is (b, t, d)); applied at layers 20-27. Base arm
    passes bias_fn=None. Returns (text, n_generated, truncated)."""
    import torch

    from stencil.qwen3 import KVCache

    ids = tok.encode(TMPL.format(p=prompt)).ids
    P = len(ids)
    cache = KVCache()
    out = []

    def make_hook(past):
        def hook(h20):
            row = bias_fn(h20, P, past)
            if row is None:
                return None
            return {layer: row for layer in WAVE_LAYERS}
        return (20, hook)

    t0 = time.monotonic()
    timed_out = False
    with torch.no_grad():
        hook = make_hook(0) if bias_fn is not None else None
        logits = m(torch.tensor([ids], device="cuda"), cache=cache, bias_hook=hook)
        nxt = int(logits[0, -1].argmax())
        while nxt not in EOS and len(out) < max_new:
            if deadline_s is not None and time.monotonic() - t0 > deadline_s:
                timed_out = True
                break
            out.append(nxt)
            hook = make_hook(cache.length) if bias_fn is not None else None
            logits = m(torch.tensor([[nxt]], device="cuda"), cache=cache, bias_hook=hook)
            nxt = int(logits[0, -1].argmax())
    return tok.decode(out), len(out), len(out) >= max_new, timed_out


def make_wave_bias_fn(ctrl, state):
    """the registered consumer adapter (v3.1/v3.2): at prefill, stash the
    prompt's h20 as ledger keys AND bias the SCORED final row from its
    own h20 (the first response token — or the loglikelihood decision
    row — is wave-influenced); per generation step, bias the current
    row over prompt positions. Same-position semantics throughout."""
    import torch

    def bias_fn(h20, P, past):
        if past == 0:
            state["K"] = h20[0, :P].float()
            row_p = ctrl(h20[0, P - 1:P].float(), state["K"])
            b = torch.zeros(P, P, device="cuda")
            b[-1, :P] = row_p[0]
            state["prefill_field"] = row_p.detach()
            return b
        row_p = ctrl(h20[0, -1:].float(), state["K"])
        row = torch.zeros(1, past + 1, device="cuda")
        row[0, :P] = row_p[0]
        return row
    return bias_fn


def wave_hook_for_prefill(ctrl, P):
    """single-forward loglikelihood variant of the adapter: returns a
    (layer, fn) bias_hook that biases only the final (scored) row."""
    import torch

    def hook(h20):
        K = h20[0, :P].float()
        row_p = ctrl(h20[0, P - 1:P].float(), K)
        b = torch.zeros(P, P, device="cuda")
        b[-1, :P] = row_p[0]
        return {layer: b for layer in WAVE_LAYERS}
    return (20, hook)


def provenance_pins(root, extra_files=()):
    """the registered resume pin set (v4.1): sha256 of trunk, tokenizer,
    the execution modules, and the vendored IFEval verifier tree, plus
    any extra files (controllers, datasets, the sealed runner)."""
    import hashlib
    from pathlib import Path as _P
    root = _P(root)
    files = [
        "models/qwen3-1.7b.pt",
        "models/qwen3-1.7b-hf/tokenizer.json",
        "src/stencil/bench.py",
        "src/stencil/qwen3.py",
        "src/stencil/wave.py",
    ]
    pins = {}
    for f in files:
        pins[f] = hashlib.sha256((root / f).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    tree = hashlib.sha256()
    for vf in sorted((root / "vendor" / "ifeval").glob("*.py")):
        tree.update(vf.read_bytes())
    pins["vendor/ifeval(tree)"] = tree.hexdigest()
    for f in extra_files:
        pins[str(f)] = hashlib.sha256((root / f).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    return pins
